Food and Money, Part 3
3
清初，漕政仍明制，用屯丁長運。 長運者，令瓜、淮兌運軍船往各州縣水次領兌民，加過江腳耗，視遠近為差； 而淮、徐、臨、德四倉仍系民運交倉者，並兌運軍船，所謂改兌者也。 逮至中葉，會通河塞，而膠萊故道又難猝復，借黃轉般諸法行之又不能無弊，於是宣宗采英和、陶澍、賀長齡諸臣議復海運，遴員集粟，由上海雇商轉船漕京師，民咸稱便。 河運自此遂廢。 夫河運剝淺有費，過閘過淮有費，催趲通倉又有費。 上既出百餘萬漕項，下復出百餘萬幫費，民生日蹙，國計益貧。 海運則不由內地，不歸眾飽，無造船之煩，無募丁之擾，利國便民，計無逾此。 洎乎海禁大開，輪舶通行，東南之粟源源而至，不待官運，於是漕運悉廢，而改徵折漕，遂為不易之經。 今敘次漕運，首漕糧，次白糧，次督運，次漕船，次錢糧，次考成，次賞恤，而以海運終焉。
In the early Qing, grain transport still followed Ming practice, relying on military colonists for long-distance hauls. Under long-distance transport, Guazhou and Huai exchange-transport fleet ships went to each county landing to take on grain from taxpayers, with river-crossing porterage and loss allowances added by distance. For the Huai, Xu, Lin, and De granaries, where the populace had formerly delivered grain, delivery was likewise assigned to exchange-transport fleet ships—the so-called changed exchange. By mid-dynasty the Grand Canal was silted shut, and the old Jiao–Lai waterway could not be reopened in haste; transshipment via the Yellow River, though tried, could not be run without abuse. The Xuanzong Emperor then took the advice of Ying He, Tao Shu, He Changling, and others to restore sea transport, appointed officials to assemble grain, and hired merchant ships at Shanghai to carry tribute grain to the capital by sea, to universal public approval. From that point river transport was abandoned. River transport incurred costs for lightening in shallows, for passing locks and the Huai crossing, and again for pressing convoys through to the granaries. The throne already disbursed over a million taels on tribute-grain accounts, while locally another million-plus taels in supplementary charges were levied; common livelihoods tightened and the treasury grew poorer. Sea transport avoided the interior, did not feed hosts of dependents along the route, and spared the trouble of building ships and the harassment of recruiting transport crews—it profited the state and eased the people; no policy was its equal. Once maritime restrictions were largely lifted and steamers came into common use, southeastern grain flowed in steadily without official convoys; tribute transport was then abolished entirely, and converting grain quotas to silver payments became the permanent arrangement. This account of grain transport proceeds in order: tribute grain, white rice, transport supervision, transport vessels, money-grain, performance review, rewards and relief, and finally sea transport.
4
漕運初悉仍明舊，有正兌、改兌、改徵、折徵。 此四者，漕運本折之大綱也。 順治二年，戶部奏定每歲額徵漕糧四百萬石。 其運京倉者為正兌米，原額三百三十萬石：江南百五十萬，浙江六十萬，江西四十萬，湖廣二十五萬，山東二十萬，河南二十七萬。 其運通漕者為改兌米，原額七十萬石：江南二十九萬四千四百，浙江三萬，江西十七萬，山東九萬五千六百，河南十一萬。 其後頗有折改。 至乾隆十八年，實徵正兌米二百七十五萬餘石，改兌米五十萬石有奇，其隨時截留蠲緩者不在其例。 山東、河南漕糧外有小麥、黑豆，兩省通徵正兌。 改耗麥六萬九千五百六十一石八斗四升有奇，豆二十萬八千一百九十九石三斗一升有奇，皆運京倉。 黑豆系粟米改徵，無定額。 凡改徵出特旨，無常例。
Grain transport at first entirely followed Ming usage, comprising regular exchange, changed exchange, changed levy, and commuted levy. These four formed the principal framework of tribute transport and commutation. In Shunzhi 2 the Board of Revenue fixed the annual tribute-grain quota at four million shi. Grain sent to Beijing granaries was regular-exchange rice, originally 3.3 million shi: Jiangnan 1.5 million, Zhejiang 600,000, Jiangxi 400,000, Huguang 250,000, Shandong 200,000, and Henan 270,000. Grain sent to Tongzhou on the canal was changed-exchange rice, originally 700,000 shi: Jiangnan 294,400, Zhejiang 30,000, Jiangxi 170,000, Shandong 95,600, and Henan 110,000. Thereafter quotas were repeatedly adjusted. By Qianlong 18 actual regular-exchange levies exceeded 2.75 million shi and changed-exchange levies somewhat over 500,000 shi, excluding ad hoc withholdings, remissions, and deferrals. Shandong and Henan also levied wheat and black beans in addition to tribute grain, both provinces assessing them with regular exchange. Changed-levy wheat totaled 69,561 shi 8 dou 4 sheng odd and beans 208,199 shi 3 dou 1 sheng odd, all sent to Beijing granaries. Black beans were commuted from millet tribute and carried no fixed quota. Changed levies were issued only by special edict, not by standing precedent.
5
折徵之目有四：曰永折，曰灰石米折，曰減徵，曰民折官辦。 永折漕糧，山東、河南各七萬石，石折銀六錢、八錢不等； 江蘇十萬六千四百九十二石有奇，石折銀六錢不等； 安徽七萬五千九百六十一石有奇，石折銀五錢至七錢不等； 湖北三萬二千五百二十石，湖南五千二百十有二石各有奇，石均折銀七錢。 其價銀統歸地丁報部。 灰石改折，江蘇二萬九千四百二十四石，浙江萬八千六百五十三石，遇閏加折四千十有五石，石折銀一兩六錢，以供工部備置灰石之用，自順治十七年始也。
Commuted levies had four categories: permanent commutation, lime-and-stone rice commutation, reduced levy, and populace silver with official purchase. Permanent-commutation tribute: Shandong and Henan each 70,000 shi, at six to eight mace of silver per shi, varying; Jiangsu 106,492 shi odd at six mace per shi; Anhui 75,961 shi odd from five to seven mace per shi; Hubei 32,520 shi and Hunan 5,212 shi odd, each at seven mace per shi. The silver was reported to the ministry together with land-and-poll tax receipts. Lime-and-stone commutation: Jiangsu 29,424 shi and Zhejiang 18,653 shi, plus 4,015 shi in intercalary years, at 1.6 taels per shi for Board of Works lime and stone, from Shunzhi 17.
6
次年，飭江南、浙江、江西三省大吏，凡改折止許照價徵收，如藉兌漕為名，濫行科索者，即行參勘。 又以蘇、松、常、鎮四府差( 每系) 賦重，漕米每石折銀一兩，其隨漕輕齎席木贈截等銀，仍徵之耗米，及給軍行月贈耗等米，亦按時價折徵。 康熙八年，定河南漕糧石折銀八錢。 九年，浙江嘉、湖二府被災，每石折徵一兩。 五十八年，覆准河南附近水次之州縣，額徵漕糧每石八錢內，節省銀一錢五分，仍令民間上納，餘六錢五分，令徵本色起運。 至距水次較遠及不近水次之州縣，額徵米石，仍依舊例徵銀八錢，以一錢五分解部，餘交糧道採辦米石。 雍正元年，以嘉、湖二屬州縣災，諭令收徵漕米本折各半，其折價依康熙九年例。 六年，議定河南去水次稍遠州縣，均徵本色，惟南陽、汝寧二府屬，河南府之盧氏、嵩、永寧三縣及光、汝二州並屬縣，又離水次最遠之靈寶、閿鄉，路遠運艱，共酌減米萬五千六十二石有奇，免其辦解，分撥內黃、濬、滑、儀封、考城等五縣協辦，於五縣地丁銀內扣除完漕，照部價每石八錢，以六錢五分辦運，節省之一錢五分，徵解糧道補項。 其南、汝等府屬，每石折銀八錢解司，以抵濬、滑等五縣地丁銀數，所謂減徵是也。
The next year grand officials of Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi were ordered that commuted levies be collected only at the fixed price; anyone extorting under the name of exchange tribute was to be impeached immediately. Because Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang ( as a rule) carried heavy assessments, tribute rice was commuted at one tael per shi; accompanying light-burden silver for mats, timber, presentation, and withholding was still charged on wastage rice, and monthly allowance and wastage rice for transport troops were commuted at market price. In Kangxi 8 Henan tribute grain was fixed at eight mace of silver per shi. In Kangxi 9 Jiaxing and Huzhou in Zhejiang, stricken by disaster, were commuted at one tael per shi. In Kangxi 58 it was approved that in Henan counties near water landings, of the eight mace per shi quota, one mace five candareens was still collected from taxpayers while the remaining six mace five candareens was levied in kind for transport. Counties farther from landings or without nearby water still paid eight mace per shi as before: one mace five candareens to the ministry, the rest to the grain intendant for purchase. In Yongzheng 1, with Jia and Hu districts stricken, an edict ordered half the tribute in kind and half commuted at the Kangxi 9 rate. In Yongzheng 6 Henan counties somewhat distant from landings were to levy in kind; only Nanyang and Runing prefectures, Lushi, Song, and Yongning counties, Guang and Ru prefectures and subordinates, and the remotest Lingbao and Minxiang—15,062 shi odd in all—were exempted from delivery and reassigned to Neihuang, Jun, Hua, Yifeng, and Kaocheng, whose land-tax silver completed the quota at eight mace per shi ministry price, six mace five for transport, the saved one mace five to the grain intendant. Nanyang, Runing, and other subordinates paid eight mace per shi to the provincial treasury to offset the five counties' land-tax silver—the so-called reduced levy.
7
乾隆二年，以大濬運河，江蘇淮安之山陽、鹽城、阜寧，揚州之江都、甘泉、高郵、寶應各
In Qianlong 2, with the Grand Canal under major dredging, tribute grain of Shanyang, Yancheng, and Funing in Huai'an, Jiangsu, and Jiangdu, Ganquan, Gaoyou, and Baoying in Yangzhou,
8
縣漕糧，每石徵折銀一兩。 其後海州、贛榆兩邑亦然。 山東、河南向所改徵黑豆，不敷支給，河南再改徵二萬石，山東四萬石。 三年，湖廣總督德霈言湖南平江距水次五百餘里，請改折色，分撥衡陽、湘潭代買兌運，從之。 七年，江西瀘溪以折價八錢不敷採買，定嗣後每年八月借司庫銀撥縣採買，照買價徵銀歸還。 其後江蘇之嘉定、寶山、海州、贛榆，安徽之寧國、旌德、太平、英山，湖北之通山、當陽諸州縣，悉遵此例。 十一年，定河南祥符等四十州縣額徵粟米內，每年改小麥萬石，與漕米黑豆並徵運通。
each county was commuted at one tael of silver per shi. Haizhou and Ganyu later followed the same rule. Commuted black beans in Shandong and Henan no longer sufficed; Henan commuted another 20,000 shi and Shandong 40,000 shi. In Qianlong 3 Huguang Governor-General De Pei reported that Pingjiang, Hunan, lay over 500 li from the landing and asked to commute to silver, with Hengyang and Xiangtan buying and shipping on its behalf; approved. In Qianlong 7 Luxi, Jiangxi, found eight mace insufficient; thereafter each August treasury silver was advanced for county purchase, with collection at actual price for repayment. Jiading, Baoshan, Haizhou, and Ganyu in Jiangsu; Ningguo, Jingde, Taiping, and Yingshan in Anhui; and Tongshan and Dangyang in Hubei later followed suit. In Qianlong 11 forty Henan prefectures and counties including Xiangfu were ordered to commute 10,000 shi of wheat yearly from millet quotas, levied with tribute rice and black beans for Tongzhou.
9
十六年，以京師官兵向養馬駝，需用黑豆，豫、東二省自雍正十年以來，於漕糧粟米內節次改徵，每年額解黑豆二十萬九千餘石，每省酌量再改徵黑豆一二萬石。 尋定山東三萬石，河南二萬石，額徵粟米，照數除抵，其節省銀一錢五分為運腳之用者並徵之。 十八年，倉場侍郎鶴年言：「現在京倉黑豆六十萬餘石，足供三年支放，請自明年始，豫、東二省應運黑豆，酌半改徵粟米，分貯京、通各倉，則豆無潮黰之虞，粟價亦平。 」從之。
In Qianlong 16, with capital troops' horse and camel fodder requiring black beans, Henan and Shandong since Yongzheng 10 had progressively commuted from tribute millet, delivering over 209,000 shi of beans yearly; each province was to commute another 10,000–20,000 shi as needed. Soon after, Shandong 30,000 and Henan 20,000 shi were fixed as millet quotas with corresponding deductions; the saved one mace five candareens for transport was also collected. In Qianlong 18 Granary Commissioner He Nian said: "Beijing granaries now hold over 600,000 shi of black beans, enough for three years. From next year let Henan and Shandong commute half their bean quota to millet for Beijing and Tongzhou stores, avoiding bean spoilage and stabilizing millet prices." Approved.
10
二十六年，以江蘇之清河、桃源、宿遷、沭陽不產米粟，命嗣後先動司庫銀兩，按照時價採辦，令民輸銀還欸，是謂民折官辦。 其後阜寧、旌德、泰興、寧國、太平、英山諸縣皆仿行之。
In Qianlong 26, because Qinghe, Taoyuan, Suqian, and Shuyang in Jiangsu grew no grain, treasury silver was to be advanced at market price for official purchase, taxpayers repaying in silver—populace commutation with official procurement. Funing, Jingde, Taixing, Ningguo, Taiping, and Yingshan later followed.
11
二十一年諭曰：「漕糧歲輸天庾，例徵本色。 勒收折色，向干嚴禁。 現值年豐穀賤，若令小民以賤價糶穀，交納折色，是閭閻終歲勤劬，所得升斗，大半糶以輸官，以有限之蓋藏，供無窮之朘削，病民實甚。 著通諭有漕省分大吏，飭所屬徵收糧米，概以本色交納，無許勒折滋弊。 如有專利虐民者，據實嚴參。 」然州縣往往仍藉改折浮收，雖有明令，莫能禁也。
In Qianlong 21 an edict said: "Tribute grain fills the imperial granaries yearly and must be levied in kind by statute. Forced commutation to silver has always been forbidden. In a year of plenty and cheap grain, forcing taxpayers to sell cheaply for commuted silver would mean most of a household's harvest sold to officials—finite stores feeding endless levies, a grave injury to the people. Grand officials of all tribute provinces are to order subordinates to collect wholly in kind and forbid forced commutation. Anyone profiteering at the people's expense is to be impeached on report. Yet counties still used commutation to pad collections; clear orders could not stop it.
12
正兌、改兌、改折之外，復有截漕及撥運。 各省截留漕船，介於起運停運之間，行月二糧，應給應追，向無定例。 自乾隆元年，議定江蘇、安徽、浙江截留漕船應支本折月糧三修銀，照數全給。 至行糧盤耗贈銀負重等項，按站發給。 若幫船截留本次，或旋兌旋卸，或數月後清，贈米亦按月計算。 江西船大載重，每年三修銀不敷，則取辦於行月二糧。 遇有截留，將原領折耗行月贈銀贈米斛面米均免扣追。 嗣以運軍掛欠之項，諭將雍正十二年以前各省截留漕船應追等項悉免之。 七年，以各省截留漕船已兌開行，例須扣追，酌定加給，視程途遠近、船糧多寡為衡。 山東、河南每船給銀五十兩。 江南、浙江六十兩，湖廣七十兩，江西九十兩，以充各軍在次修船置備器具，及雇募舵工水手安家養贍之用。 其應給之銀，即於行月折色銀內扣給。 十八年，諭曰：「前命截留南漕二十萬分貯天津水次各倉備用，但恐旗丁等於米色斛面任意攙和短少，而州縣胥役又往往藉端勒索，令方觀承飭天津道親往監看。 嗣後截漕之省，俱派就近道員稽查，不得委州縣。 著為令。 」
Beyond regular exchange, changed exchange, and commutation there were also tribute withholding and allocated transport. When provinces detained transport ships between departure and halt, two months' ration allowances due and recoverable had no fixed precedent. From Qianlong 1 detained ships in Jiangsu, Anhui, and Zhejiang received full monthly grain in kind and silver plus three-repair silver. Travel grain, wastage silver, and heavy-load allowances were paid by station. If escort ships were held for the current run—whether unloaded at once or cleared months later—presentation rice was reckoned monthly. Jiangxi ships were large; when three-repair silver ran short, the shortfall came from two months' travel grain. When ships were detained, commuted wastage, travel presentation silver, presentation rice, and surface rice already issued were not recovered. Later, regarding transport troops' arrears, an edict remitted all recoveries on ships detained before Yongzheng 12. In Qianlong 7, with detained ships already exchanged and under way, recovery was required by rule but supplemental grants were fixed by distance and load. Shandong and Henan: fifty taels per ship. Jiangnan and Zhejiang sixty, Huguang seventy, Jiangxi ninety—for repair and outfitting at the landing and hiring crews for settlement and upkeep. Grants were deducted from commuted travel-month silver. In Qianlong 18 an edict said: "I earlier ordered 20,000 shi of southern tribute withheld at Tianjin landing granaries, but feared banner crews might adulterate grain and clerks extort—Fang Guancheng is to supervise in person. Henceforth provinces withholding tribute must assign the nearest circuit intendant to inspect, not prefectures or counties. Let this stand as regulation. (Close of edict.)
13
撥運者，截留山東、河南所運薊州糧，撥充陵糈及駐防兵米者也。 康熙三十四年，議定年需粟米三萬六百餘石，將山東漕糧粟米照數截留，以原船自天津運至新河口，撥天津紅剝船百五十艘，運至薊州五里橋，船載百石，每百里給腳價一兩三錢二分，所需之銀，於過閘入倉腳價內撥給。 四十五年，定密雲駐防兵米，在豫、東二省每年徵存薊糧項下撥運，令該縣於春夏之交，赴通領運收倉。 平時由水運，有故則陸運。 腳價由地糧銀內給發。 次年，令豫、東各添撥米百石，備支銷折耗。 又撥運保定、雄縣兩處駐防兵米，截至西沽就船受兌，以節耗費。 嘉慶初，因東省輪免漕糧，先令豫省兌運，不敷之數，許動支節年倉存薊米，並動碾公穀。 其後河南被災，亦准在薊倉存米存穀內碾動。 其各州縣派撥之數，薊州五萬八千六百石、易州三萬八千六百石各有奇，密雲一萬一千五百餘石，保定、雄縣共三千一百餘石，良鄉暨大興之采育三百餘石，順義、昌平二百餘石，霸州、東安、固安、寶坻三百餘石，玉田及遷安之冷口各五百餘石，滄州二千七百餘石。 又青州駐防兵米二千一百餘石，亦於薊糧內截留運供，德州駐防兵米不敷，亦得動支。 此撥運之大略也。
Allocated transport withheld Shandong and Henan grain bound for Jizhou and reassigned it for imperial tombs and garrison rations. In Kangxi 34 yearly need was fixed at 30,600 shi odd of millet; Shandong tribute millet was withheld accordingly, carried from Tianjin to Xinhekou on the original fleet, then 150 Tianjin red-boats to Wuliqiao, Jizhou, 100 shi per boat at 1.32 taels per hundred li from lock-and-granary porterage funds. In Kangxi 45 Miyun garrison grain was drawn from Henan and Shandong Jizhou reserves; counties were to draw at Tongzhou in spring and summer for granary delivery. Normally by water; when blocked, by land. Porterage came from land-tax silver. The next year Henan and Shandong each added 100 shi for wastage. Baoding and Xiongxian garrison grain was allocated, taken on ship at Xigu to reduce loss. Early Jiaqing, with Shandong rotating tribute exemptions, Henan transported first; shortfalls could use stored Jizhou grain and public stocks. When Henan later suffered disaster, milling from Jizhou stores was also allowed. County allocations: Jizhou 58,600 shi odd, Yizhou 38,600 shi odd, Miyun 11,500 shi odd, Baoding and Xiongxian 3,100 shi odd, Liangxiang and Daxing Caiyu 300 shi odd, Shunyi and Changping 200 shi odd, Bazhou, Dong'an, Gu'an, and Baodi 300 shi odd, Yutian and Qian'an Lengkou 500 shi odd each, Cangzhou 2,700 shi odd. Qingzhou garrison's 2,100 shi odd was also taken from Jizhou grain; Dezhou garrison shortfalls could draw on stores. Such is the general outline of allocated transport.
14
各省之徵收漕糧也，向系軍民交兌，運軍往往勒索擾民。 順治九年，始改為官收官兌，酌定贈貼銀米，隨漕徵收，官為支給。 雍正六年，以江、浙應納漕糧為額甚巨，若必拘定粳米，恐價昂難於輸將，以後但擇乾圓潔淨，准紅白兼收，秈稉並納，著為令。 乾隆初，奏定民納漕米，隨到隨收，嚴禁蠹書留難。 四年，諭曰：「朕聞湖北糧米，以十五萬一千餘石運赴通倉，名曰北漕，十二萬六千餘石為荊州官米，名曰南漕，二項原可合收分解。 乃有不肖州縣，分設倉口，令糧戶依兩處完納，以圖多得贏餘，重累吾民。 著行文該省，將二項漕糧合收，永遠遵行。 」七年，定直省有漕各屬，於隔歲年終，刊易知由單，條悉開載，按戶分給，以杜濫科。 十年，工部侍郎范燦奏：「江南下江徵收漕米，向借漕費之名，或九折，或八折，自巡撫尹繼善定每石收費六分，諸弊盡革。 久之，吏胥復乘緊兌之際，多方刁難，小民勢難久待，不得不議扣折。 」諭飭有漕省分大小官吏，嚴行釐剔積弊。 嘉慶八年，禁止各州縣漕糧私收折色，及刁生劣監收攬包交。
Provincial tribute collection had been military–populace exchange, transport troops often extorting taxpayers. In Shunzhi 9 this became official collection and official exchange; presentation and subsidy silver and grain were fixed, levied with tribute, and paid by officials. In Yongzheng 6, with huge Jiangsu and Zhejiang quotas, strict glutinous-rice requirements were eased: only clean, sound grain was required—red or white, husked or glutinous—by regulation. Early Qianlong memorials ordered tribute received as delivered, clerks forbidden to delay. In Qianlong 4 an edict said: "Hubei ships 151,000 shi odd to Tongzhou as northern tribute and 126,000 shi odd as Jingzhou southern tribute—the two could be collected and split together. Yet corrupt officials set up separate granaries and made households pay twice for surplus—greatly burdening taxpayers. Order Hubei to combine collection permanently. In Qianlong 7 all tribute districts in metropolitan provinces were to issue plain notice slips by year's end, itemized and distributed by household, to stop irregular levies. In Qianlong 10 Works Vice Minister Fan Can said: "Lower Jiangnan tribute had been collected at nine- or eight-tenths under transport-fee pretexts until Governor Yin Jishan fixed six fen per shi and ended abuses. In time clerks again obstructed at urgent exchange; taxpayers could not wait and had to accept deductions. " An edict ordered all tribute officials to eliminate accumulated abuses strictly. In the eighth year of the Jiaqing reign (1803), the government prohibited prefectures and counties from privately collecting cash commutation on grain-transport levies and barred scheming literati and corrupt grain supervisors from monopolizing collection and bundling deliveries under contract.
15
凡漕糧皆隨以耗費，耗皆以米，正兌一石耗二斗五升至四斗，改兌一石耗一斗七升至四斗，皆隨正入倉，以供京、通各倉並漕運折耗之用。 其南糧又有隨船作耗米，自五升至二升三升不等，以途之遠近為差。 嘉慶間，定江蘇漕糧耗米原備篩颺，耗米四升有奇。 嗣後以二升餘劃付旗丁，二升隨糧交倉。 浙江、江西、兩湖悉依此例。 逮漕務改章，凡改徵折色各省，耗米亦折價與正米並徵，自是漕耗之名遂廢。
Every grain-transport levy carried a wastage allowance paid in grain. Direct delivery permitted two and a half to four dou per picul; converted delivery permitted one and seven-tenths to four dou per picul. These allowances entered the granaries with the principal grain to supply Beijing and Tongzhou stores and to cover transport losses. Southern shipments also included shipboard wastage grain, ranging from two or three sheng up to five sheng depending on the distance traveled. During the Jiaqing reign, Jiangsu fixed the grain-transport wastage allowance at just over four sheng per picul, originally intended to cover winnowing and screening. Subsequently, a little over two sheng was allotted to banner transport crews and two sheng was delivered to the granary with the principal grain. Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and the two Hu provinces all followed this rule. When grain-transport regulations were revised, provinces that converted collection to cash commutation also commuted wastage allowances and collected them together with the principal grain, and the category of grain-transport wastage was abolished.
16
初，各省漕糧改為官收官兌，贈貼名稱，山東、河南謂之潤耗，江蘇、安徽謂之漕貼，浙江謂之漕截，江西、兩湖謂之貼運，其數多寡不一，隨糧徵給，均刊列易知由單，私派挪移者罪之。 其後江南每糧百石，竟私截至百餘兩，浙江至三十餘兩。 糧道劉朝俊以貪婪漕貼萬二千餘兩被劾，給事中徐旭齡亦疏陳贈耗之弊。 然貪官污吏，積習相沿，莫能禁也。 康熙十年，議定江寧等府起運耗米及正糧一體貼贈，蘇、松、常三府改折灰石，幫貼漕折等銀悉免之。 二十四年，令各省隨漕截銀免解道庫，徑令州縣給發。 乾隆七年，定江南漕米贈耗永免停支例。 各省收漕州縣，除隨正耗米及運軍行月糧本折漕贈等項外，別收漕耗銀米，其數亦多寡不一，此項耗外之米，皆供官軍兌漕雜費及州縣辦公之用者也。
When provincial grain-transport levies were placed under official collection and delivery, supplementary grants took different names—moistening wastage in Shandong and Henan, grain-transport subsidy in Jiangsu and Anhui, grain-transport deduction in Zhejiang, and transport subsidy in Jiangxi and the two Hu provinces. Amounts varied by region, were collected and disbursed with the grain, were listed on standardized receipt slips, and private surcharges or diversions were criminal offenses. In Jiangnan, private deductions on every hundred piculs of grain eventually exceeded a hundred taels; in Zhejiang they exceeded thirty taels. Grain intendant Liu Chaojun was impeached for embezzling more than twelve thousand taels in grain-transport subsidies, and censor Xu Xuling also memorialized detailing abuses in supplementary wastage payments. Yet corrupt officials, entrenched in long-standing abuses, could not be stopped. In the tenth year of the Kangxi reign (1671), Jiangning and other prefectures were required to grant shipping wastage and principal grain together; Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou were switched to commutation in lime and stone, and all supplementary silver for grain-transport commutation was abolished. In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi (1685), each province was ordered to exempt grain-transport deduction silver from remittance to the intendant treasury and to disburse it directly through prefectures and counties. In the seventh year of the Qianlong reign (1742), Jiangnan grain-transport supplementary wastage was permanently exempted from the precedent of suspension. In grain-collecting prefectures and counties across the provinces, beyond wastage grain accompanying the principal levy, transport troops monthly rations, and commuted grain-transport supplementary grants, additional grain-transport wastage in silver and grain was collected in varying amounts. This extra wastage supplied miscellaneous costs of official and military grain delivery and prefectural and county administration.
17
輕齎銀者，始於有明中葉。 以諸倉兌運，須給路費，徵耗米，兌運米一平一銳，其銳米量取隨船作耗，餘皆折銀，名曰輕齎。 清因之。 每年正兌米一石，江西、兩湖諸省加耗四斗六升或六斗六升，銳米皆一斗。 加耗四斗六升者，則以三斗隨船作耗，而以連銳二斗六升折銀一錢三分； 加耗六斗六升者，則以四斗隨船作耗，而以連銳三斗六升折銀一錢八分，謂之三六輕齎。 江蘇、安徽每石加耗五斗六升，銳米一斗，除四斗隨船作耗，而以餘米二斗六升折銀一錢三分，謂之二六輕齎。 山東、河南每石加耗三升，銳米一斗，除二斗五升隨船作耗，餘米一斗六升折銀八分，謂之一六輕齎。 其改兌止有耗米，或三斗二升至一斗七升不等，止給本色隨船作耗，而以存米二升易銀一分，謂之折易輕齎。 均每升折徵銀五釐，解倉場通濟庫。 康熙四十七年，令每年江南等省額解輕齎銀三十八萬四千兩，內除山東、河南、湖廣、江西、浙江、江南等省額解銀二十四萬六千九百餘兩，仍留通濟庫應用，其蘇松糧道所屬額解銀十三萬七千餘兩，徑解戶部。 如倉場不敷，得咨行戶部支發。 尋分撥蘇松糧道所屬額解輕齎銀五萬分解通濟庫備用。 用此項輕齎銀，例應兌漕通以濟運務，外此有席木竹板等存，皆隨漕交納，其尺寸長短廣狹，均有定制。
The "light carriage" silver payment originated in the mid-Ming period. Because granary deliveries required road expenses and wastage grain, transport grain was measured as one level picul and one sharp picul; the sharp portion covered shipboard wastage and the remainder was commuted to silver, called light carriage. The Qing dynasty retained the practice. Each year, for every picul of direct-delivery grain, Jiangxi, the two Hu provinces, and other provinces added either four dou six sheng or six dou six sheng in wastage; the sharp portion was always one dou. Where wastage of four dou six sheng was added, three dou served as shipboard wastage and, together with the sharp grain, two dou six sheng were commuted to one mace and three candareens of silver. Where wastage of six dou six sheng was added, four dou served as shipboard wastage and, together with the sharp grain, three dou six sheng were commuted to one mace and eight candareens of silver—the three-six light carriage. Jiangsu and Anhui added five dou six sheng wastage per picul with one dou of sharp grain; after four dou for shipboard wastage, the remaining two dou six sheng were commuted to one mace and three candareens of silver—the two-six light carriage. Shandong and Henan added three sheng wastage per picul with one dou of sharp grain; after two dou five sheng for shipboard wastage, the remaining one dou six sheng were commuted to eight candareens of silver—the one-six light carriage. Converted delivery involved only wastage grain, ranging from three dou two sheng down to one dou seven sheng; only principal grain was issued for shipboard wastage, and the remaining two sheng were exchanged for one fen of silver—the commutation light carriage. In every case, each sheng was commuted and collected at five candareens of silver and remitted to the Tongji Treasury at the granary depot. In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi (1708), Jiangnan and other provinces were ordered to remit a quota of 384,000 taels in light-carriage silver annually. Of this, the 246,900-odd taels remitted by Shandong, Henan, Huguang, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and other provinces remained at the Tongji Treasury, while the 137,000-odd taels under the Suzhou-Songjiang grain intendant were remitted directly to the Board of Revenue. If the granary depot lacked funds, officials could request disbursement from the Board of Revenue. Soon afterward, 50,000 taels of the Suzhou-Songjiang grain intendant quota light-carriage silver was allocated to the Tongji Treasury as a reserve. This light-carriage silver was by regulation used for grain delivery at Tongzhou to support transport operations. Beyond that, stored mats, timber, bamboo boards, and similar supplies were delivered with each shipment, all to prescribed dimensions.
18
道光二十九年，兩江總督李星沅奏南漕改折，戶部定價太輕，開不肖州縣浮勒之端。 江蘇巡撫陸建瀛亦言其不便。 遂罷改徵折色。 同治四年，曾國籓、李鴻章請將江蘇鎮洋、太倉二州縣漕糧改徵折色，不許。 光緒十年，翰林院侍讀王邦璽疏陳丁漕有五弊、三難、五宜、三不可。 是時直省丁漕積欠頻仍，故邦璽以為言。 二十三年，侍講學士瑞洵言南漕改折，有益無損。 先是江、浙漕米，除河運十二三萬石外，歲約海運百二十餘萬。 二十年，辦理海防，江、浙各省各折十之五六。 翌年，兩江總督張之洞擬令蘇省州縣收折收本仍其舊，而由官全行折解。 部令仍運本色。 張之洞復奏，蘇漕全折，歲可省運費八十萬，浙江全折，兩湖採買全停，剝船挑河各費、漕職衛官各項，均可酌減，歲可省百五十萬。 嗣戶部以庫儲支絀，請將江蘇海運漕糧暫減運三十萬石，得銀九十八萬餘兩。 奕劻等奏言：「南漕歲有定額，兵民生計攸關，京師根本重地，尤須寬為儲備。 言者動稱折漕歲五六百萬，實則不過百餘萬有奇，似不宜輕議更張。 」從之。
In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang (1849), Governor-General Li Xingyuan of the Two Jiangs memorialized that southern grain transport had been converted to cash commutation, but the Board of Revenue fixed price was too low and invited extortion by unscrupulous prefectures and counties. Jiangsu Governor Lu Jianying also argued that the arrangement was impractical. Commutation collection was therefore abolished. In the fourth year of Tongzhi (1865), Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang requested that grain-transport levies in Zhenjiang and Taicang in Jiangsu be converted to cash commutation; the request was denied. In the tenth year of Guangxu (1884), Hanlin Reader Wang Bangxi memorialized that corvée and grain transport suffered five abuses, three difficulties, five recommended reforms, and three prohibitions. At the time, direct provinces were plagued by repeated corvée and grain-transport arrears, which prompted Wang Bangxi memorial. In the twenty-third year of Guangxu (1897), Hanlin Reader Rui Xun argued that converting southern grain transport to cash commutation would benefit the system without harm. Previously, aside from 120,000 to 130,000 piculs shipped by canal, Jiangsu and Zhejiang sent roughly 1.2 million piculs of grain transport grain by sea each year. In the twentieth year of Guangxu (1894), while managing coastal defense, Jiangsu and Zhejiang each commuted five or six tenths of their shipments to cash. The following year, Governor-General Zhang Zhidong of the Two Jiangs proposed that Suzhou prefectures and counties continue collecting commutation or grain in kind as before while the government commuted and remitted the full amount. The Board ordered that grain in kind continue to be transported. Zhang Zhidong memorialized again: full commutation of Jiangsu grain transport could save 800,000 taels in transport costs each year; full commutation in Zhejiang and cessation of procurement in the two Hu provinces could reduce lighterage, canal dredging, grain-transport officials, guards, and related expenses by roughly 1.5 million taels annually. Thereafter, citing strained treasury reserves, the Board of Revenue requested temporarily reducing Jiangsu sea-transport grain shipments by 300,000 picul, yielding more than 980,000 taels in silver. Yikuang and others memorialized: "Southern grain transport has a fixed annual quota on which soldiers and civilians depend; the capital, as the empire foundation, requires ample reserves above all. Advocates often claim that commuted grain transport would yield five or six million taels a year; in reality it would amount to little more than one million taels—too slight a gain to justify overturning the established system. The proposal was approved.
19
漕糧之外，江蘇蘇、松、常三府，太倉一州，浙江嘉、湖兩府，歲輸糯米於內務府，以供上用及百官廩祿之需，謂之白糧。 原額正米二十一萬七千四百七十二石有奇。 耗米，蘇、松、常三府，太倉一州每石加耗三斗，以五升或三升隨正米起交，餘隨船作耗，共二萬七百七石有奇； 嘉、湖二府每石加耗四斗，以五升或三升隨正米起交，餘隨船作耗，共萬三千四百八十八石有奇。 康熙初，定白糧概徵本色，惟光祿寺改折三萬石，石徵銀一兩五錢。 十四年，議定江南白糧仿浙省例，抽選漕船裝運，每船給行月糧米六十九石三斗，銀五十六兩七錢六分。 經費銀，浙江舊例四百五十七兩一錢一釐，議減去銀百二十六兩二錢四分、米二十八石。 嗣以運漕、運白事同一體，裁江、浙白糧經費，仿漕糧之例，支給行贈銀兩。 至白糧悉系包米運送，並無折耗，俟抵通照例交收。
Beyond grain-transport levies, Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou in Jiangsu, Taicang subprefecture, and Jiaxing and Huzhou in Zhejiang annually delivered glutinous rice to the Imperial Household Department for imperial consumption and official grain salaries—known as white grain. The original quota of principal grain was 217,472 piculs and a fraction. Wastage grain: in Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Taicang, each picul carried three dou of wastage; five or three sheng were delivered with the principal grain at shipment and the remainder as shipboard wastage, totaling 20,707 piculs and a fraction. In Jiaxing and Huzhou, each picul carried four dou of wastage; five or three sheng were delivered with the principal grain at shipment and the remainder as shipboard wastage, totaling 13,488 piculs and a fraction. In the early Kangxi reign, white grain was generally collected in kind; only the Court of Imperial Sacrifices commuted 30,000 picul at one tael and five mace of silver per picul. In the fourteenth year of Kangxi (1675), Jiangnan white grain was ordered to follow the Zhejiang precedent, using selected grain-transport boats; each boat received 69 piculs and three dou in monthly transport grain and 56 taels, 7 mace, and 6 candareens in silver. Expense silver: Zhejiang old quota was 457 taels, 1 mace, and 1 candareen; officials decided to cut 126 taels, 2 mace, and 4 candareens in silver and 28 piculs in grain. Thereafter, since grain-transport and white-grain shipments were treated as a single operation, Jiangsu and Zhejiang cut white-grain expense funds and, following the grain-transport precedent, disbursed transport supplementary silver instead. White grain was shipped entirely as contracted grain with no commuted wastage; upon arrival at Tongzhou it was received according to regulation.
20
先是江、浙輸將白糧二十二萬餘石，太常寺、光祿寺各賓館需用二千餘石，王公官員俸約需十五六萬石，內務府、紫禁城兵卒及內監食用需一萬石，尚餘五萬石。 乾隆二年，高宗謂：「光祿寺等處收支，原以供祭祀及賓館之用，在所必需。 其王公百官俸米，應用白糧酌減其半，以粳米抵充。 至賚賞禁城兵卒及內監米石，應將白糧易以粳米，以紓民力。 」自是實徵白糯不過十萬石有奇矣。 又准松江、太倉額徵白糯，改徵漕糧，即在派運白米十萬石內通融盈縮，以均應減應運之數。 浙江向不產糯，白糧中糯米一項，隨漕統徵糙粳，官為易糯兌運。 兩省白糧經費前已議裁，至是復照舊例徵收。 江蘇徵銀十八萬六千九百八十五兩有奇，米萬八千八百八十九石有奇，舂辦米二萬一千三百九十九石有奇，浙江徵銀四萬五千七十五兩有奇，米三千九百六十九石，舂辦米萬三千二百九十石有奇，共實徵銀二十三萬二千六十一兩，米五萬五千七百四十八石有奇。 除給運弁運軍、並解通濟庫為運送京、通各倉腳價之用，餘銀及米折，均造冊送部酌撥。 逮嘉慶中，白糧經費，江蘇徵銀六萬餘兩，米及舂辦米各萬餘石，浙江徵銀五萬餘兩，米三千餘石，舂辦米萬餘石，共實徵銀十一萬四千五百十八兩有奇，米五萬三千七百二十九石有奇，較之乾隆時經費銀所減又逾半矣。
Previously, Jiangsu and Zhejiang delivered more than 220,000 piculs of white grain: over 2,000 piculs for the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and its guest houses; about 150,000 to 160,000 piculs for princes, nobles, and officials grain salaries; 10,000 piculs for the Imperial Household Department, Forbidden City soldiers, and eunuchs; with 50,000 piculs still remaining. In the second year of Qianlong (1737), the Qianlong Emperor said: "The income and expenditures of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and related offices serve sacrifices and guest houses and are indispensable. The white-grain salaries of princes and officials should be cut by half and replaced with polished rice. Grain rations for Forbidden City soldiers and eunuchs should be supplied in polished rice instead of white grain, to ease the burden on the people. Thereafter, actual collection of white glutinous rice did not exceed 100,000 piculs and a fraction. Songjiang and Taicang were also permitted to convert their quota of white glutinous rice to grain-transport levies, adjusting flexibly within the allotted 100,000 piculs of dispatched white grain to balance required reductions and shipments. Zhejiang did not produce glutinous rice; the glutinous portion of white grain was collected together with grain transport as coarse and polished rice, which the government exchanged for glutinous rice before shipment. White-grain expense funds in both provinces had previously been slated for reduction; at this point collection reverted to the old precedent. Jiangsu collected 186,985 taels and a fraction in silver, 18,889 piculs and a fraction in grain, and 21,399 piculs and a fraction in processed grain; Zhejiang collected 45,075 taels and a fraction in silver, 3,969 piculs in grain, and 13,290 piculs and a fraction in processed grain—for a combined total of 232,061 taels in silver and 55,748 piculs and a fraction in grain. After paying transport officers and troops and remitting funds to the Tongji Treasury for porterage to Beijing and Tongzhou granaries, remaining silver and commuted grain were compiled in registers and sent to the Board for allocation. By the Jiaqing period, white-grain expenses had fallen to over 60,000 taels and over 10,000 piculs each of grain and processed grain in Jiangsu, and over 50,000 taels, over 3,000 piculs of grain, and over 10,000 piculs of processed grain in Zhejiang—a combined total of 114,518 taels and a fraction in silver and 53,729 piculs and a fraction in grain, more than half below Qianlong-era expense silver.
21
江、浙之運白糧也，初沿明代民運之制。 嗣以臨期雇募民船，時日稽遲，改行官運； 仍不便民，乃令漕船分帶，以省官民之累。 康熙三年，定浙江行漕帶法，需船百二十六艘，於漕幫內抽出六十二艘裝運，增造六十四艘併入僉運，後江蘇亦踵行之。 每船裝運五百石，擇軍船殷實堅固者裝運，五年一易。 制定每年未兌之前，責令糧道赴次查驗，如運軍力疲、船不堅固者，別選殷軍補運。 十六年，漕運總督瑚寶奏：「江蘇運白糧船向例五年更調，但為時過久，請依漕船三年抽調例，定運白三年即行另選。 」從之。 江、浙兩省運白糧船，原定蘇州、太倉為一幫，松江、常州各為一幫，嘉興、湖州各一幫，領運千總每幫二，隨幫武舉一。 改行官運後，以府通判為總部，縣丞、典史為協部，吏典為押運。 旋裁押運。 後白糧改令漕船帶運，復裁總、協二部。 蘇、松、常每府增設千總二，更番領運，每幫設隨幫百總一，押趲回空。 浙江增設千總四、隨幫二，蘇州、太倉倉運白糧船，原定百十八艘，船多軍眾，分為前後兩幫，增設千總二、隨幫一。 白糧減徵後，並兩幫為一，其千總隨幫悉予裁減。
Jiangsu and Zhejiang initially transported white grain under the Ming system of civilian conveyance. Later, because hiring civilian boats at the last moment caused delays, the system was changed to official transport. This still burdened the people, so grain-transport boats were ordered to carry white grain as well, sparing both officials and civilians. In the third year of Kangxi (1664), Zhejiang fixed the piggyback transport method, requiring 126 boats: 62 drawn from the grain-transport fleet and 64 newly built boats merged into contract transport. Jiangsu later followed suit. Each boat carried 500 piculs; sturdy military boats were selected and replaced every five years. Each year before delivery, the grain intendant was required to inspect boats at the berth; exhausted transport troops or unsound boats were replaced with sturdy crews. In the sixteenth year of Kangxi (1677), Grain Transport Governor-General Hu Bao memorialized: "Jiangsu white-grain transport boats were rotated every five years by precedent, but that interval was too long; please follow the three-year rotation rule for grain-transport boats and reselect white-grain boats every three years. The proposal was approved. White-grain transport boats in Jiangsu and Zhejiang were originally organized as one fleet for Suzhou and Taicang, one each for Songjiang and Changzhou, and one each for Jiaxing and Huzhou, with two leading ensigns and one military licentiate per fleet. Under official transport, the prefectural vice magistrate served as chief coordinator, assistant magistrates and clerical officials as deputies, and clerical functionaries as escort supervisors. Escort supervisors were soon abolished. Later, when white grain was assigned to grain-transport boats, the chief and deputy coordinator posts were abolished as well. Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou each added two ensigns who rotated as transport leaders; each fleet also gained a hundred-man ensign to escort and hurry empty return boats. Zhejiang added four ensigns and two fleet attendants. Suzhou and Taicang 118 white-grain boats, with their large crews, were split into front and rear fleets, adding two ensigns and one fleet attendant. After white-grain levies were reduced, the two fleets were merged into one and their ensigns and fleet attendants were abolished.
22
清初，都運漕糧官吏，參酌明制。 總理漕事者為漕運總督。 分轄則有糧儲道。 監兌押運則有同知、通判。 趲運則有沿河鎮道將領等官。 漕運總督駐淮南，掌僉選運弁、修造漕船、派撥全單、兌運開幫、過淮盤掣、催趲重運、查驗回空、覈勘漂流、督催漕欠諸務，其直隸、山東、河南、江西、江南、浙江、湖廣七省文武官吏經理漕務者皆屬焉。 糧道，山東、江安、蘇松、江西、浙江、湖北、湖南各一。 河南以開歸鹽驛道兼理。 糧道掌通省糧儲，統轄有司軍衛，遴委領運隨幫各官，責令各府清軍官會同運弁、僉選運軍。 兌竣，親督到淮，不得委丞倅代押。 如有軍需緊要事件，須詳明督撫、漕臣，方許委員代行其職務。
In the early Qing, officials overseeing grain-transport levies adapted the Ming system. Overall supervision of grain transport fell to the Grain Transport Governor-General. Regional jurisdiction belonged to grain storage intendants. Delivery supervision and transport escort duties fell to subprefectural magistrates and vice magistrates. Transport was hurried along by river-route garrison commanders, generals, and similar officials. The Grain Transport Governor-General was stationed at Huainan, overseeing selection of transport officers, repair of grain-transport boats, allocation of shipping orders, delivery and fleet departures, inspection at the Huai crossing, urging laden shipments, inspecting empty return boats, investigating drift losses, and pursuing transport arrears. All civil and military officials in Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Jiangxi, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and Huguang responsible for grain transport answered to him. There was one grain intendant each for Shandong, Jiangan, Suzhou-Songjiang, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Hubei, and Hunan. Henan Kaigui Salt and Post Intendant held concurrent responsibility for grain transport. The grain intendant managed provincial grain storage, commanded local officials and military guards, appointed leading transport and fleet-attendant officials, and required each prefecture grain-clearing officials to join transport officers in selecting transport troops. After delivery was complete, he personally supervised arrival at the Huai and could not delegate the escort to assistant magistrates. In urgent military supply matters, he had to report in detail to the governor-general, governor, and grain transport official before a commissioner could act in his stead.
23
監兌，舊以推官任之。 推官裁，改委同知、通判。 山東以武定同知，東昌清軍同知，濟南、兗州、泰安、曹州四通判，濟寧、臨清兩直隸州同； 河南以歸德、衛輝、懷慶三通判； 江南以江寧、蘇州督糧同知，松江董漕同知，鳳陽同知，蘇州、揚州、廬州、太平、池州、寧國、安慶、常州八管糧通判，太倉州臨時添委丞倅一； 浙江以湖州同知，杭州局糧通判，嘉興通判； 江西以南昌、吉安、臨江三通判； 淮北、湘南每年於通省同知、通判內詳委三員，監兌。 江西、湖廣、安徽監兌押淮之員尋裁。
Delivery supervision had formerly been the duty of the pushing official. When pushing officials were abolished, the duty passed to subprefectural magistrates and vice magistrates. In Shandong, delivery supervisors included the Wuding subprefectural magistrate, the Dongchang grain-clearing subprefectural magistrate, vice magistrates of Jinan, Yanzhou, Taian, and Caozhou, and subprefectural magistrates of the directly administered prefectures of Jining and Linqing. Henan assigned the three vice magistrates of Guide, Weihui, and Huaqing. Jiangnan assigned the Jiangning and Suzhou grain-supervising subprefectural magistrates, the Songjiang grain-transport supervising subprefectural magistrate, the Fengyang subprefectural magistrate, grain-managing vice magistrates of Suzhou, Yangzhou, Luzhou, Taiping, Chizhou, Ningguo, Anqing, and Changzhou, and a temporarily appointed assistant magistrate for Taicang. Zhejiang assigned the Huzhou subprefectural magistrate, the Hangzhou bureau-grain vice magistrate, and the Jiaxing vice magistrate. Jiangxi assigned the three vice magistrates of Nanchang, Jian, and Linjiang. North of the Huai and south of the Xiang, three subprefectural magistrates or vice magistrates were detailed each year from the province to supervise delivery. The Jiangxi, Huguang, and Anhui officials who supervised delivery and escorted transport at the Huai were soon abolished.
24
凡開兌，監兌官須坐守水次，將正耗行月搭運等米，逐船兌足，驗明米色純潔，面交押運官。 糧船開行，仍親督到淮，聽總漕盤驗。 糧數不足、米色不純者，罪之。 道、府、廳不揭報，照失察例議處。 意存袒護，照徇庇例議處。
Whenever exchange opened, the exchange supervisor had to stay at the landing, fill each boat with regular grain, wastage, monthly allowance, and supplementary transport rice, verify purity of grain, and deliver it in person to the escort officer. When the grain boats departed, he still personally supervised them to the Huai for inspection by the grand grain transport commissioner. Insufficient quantities or impure grain were punishable. Circuit, prefectural, and grain-office officials who failed to report them were punished under the regulations for negligent oversight. Those who intended to shield wrongdoers were punished under the regulations for favoritism and concealment.
25
押運本糧道之職，但糧道在南董理運務，無暇兼顧。 江、浙各糧道，止令督押到淮盤驗，即回任所。 總漕會同巡撫遴委管糧通判一，專司督押，約束運軍，防範侵盜攙和等弊。 山東、河南通判各一，江南七，浙江三，江西二，湖北、湖南各一。 後因通判官卑職微，復令糧道押運。 其漕船回空，仍令通判管押。 過淮必依定限，如有遲誤，照重運違限例議處。 江南、浙江、江西尋復通判押運之制。
Escorting transport was originally the grain intendant's duty, but southern intendants, fully occupied managing transport affairs, could not attend to it as well. In Jiangsu and Zhejiang each grain intendant was ordered only to escort grain to the Huai for inspection, then return to his post. The grand grain transport commissioner, together with the governor, selected one grain-assistant magistrate to supervise escort exclusively, restrain transport troops, and guard against theft, adulteration, and similar abuses. Shandong and Henan each had one; Jiangnan seven, Zhejiang three, Jiangxi two, and Hubei and Hunan one each. Later, because assistant magistrates were too low in rank and authority, escort duty was again assigned to grain intendants. When tribute boats returned empty, assistant magistrates again managed the escort. Crossing the Huai had to meet fixed deadlines; delays were punished under the regulations for heavy-transport deadline violations. Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi soon restored assistant-magistrate escort.
26
押運同知、通判抵通後，出具糧米無虧印結，由倉場侍郎送部引見。 糧道押運三次，亦准督撫咨倉場侍郎送部引見。 其員弁紳董隨同押運到通，並准擇尤保獎，以昭激勸。 其後各省大吏往往藉漕運保舉私人，朝廷亦無由究詰也。
After escorting subprefects and assistant magistrates reached Tongzhou, they issued sealed certificates of no grain loss; the granary superintendent then sent them to the ministry for audience. Grain intendants who had escorted transport three times were likewise permitted, on recommendation from governor-generals or governors, to be sent by the granary superintendent to the ministry for audience. Military officers, gentry directors, and others who accompanied escort to Tongzhou could also be singled out for commendation and reward as encouragement. Thereafter provincial grand officials often used grain transport to recommend private connections, and the court had no way to investigate.
27
淮北、淮南沿河鎮道將領，遇漕船入境，各按汛地驅行，如催趲不力，聽所在督撫糾彈。 江南京口、瓜洲渡江相對處，令鎮江道督率文武官吏催促，並令總兵官巡視河干，協催過江。 總兵裁，改由副將管理。 雍正三年，巡漕御史張坦麟條上北漕事宜：一，自通抵津，沿河舊汛窵遠，請照旱汛五里之例，漕船到汛，催漕官弁坐視阻抵不行申報者，依催趲不力例參處； 一，沿途疏淺約十三四處，坐糧廳難以兼顧，請交各汛弁率役疏通，應銷錢糧，仍令坐糧廳管理。 從之。 巡漕御史伊喇齊疏劾河南糧道提催之弊，巡撫尹繼善亦疏請革除各州縣呈送監兌押運官役陋規。 凡漕船回空到省，未開兌之前，責成本省巡撫及糧道，既開兌出境，則責成漕督及沿途文武官吏，抵津後，責成倉場侍郎、坐糧廳及天津總兵、通州副將，嚴行稽查。 有違犯者，捕獲懲治。
Along the Huai north and south banks, when tribute boats entered their sectors, garrison commanders and circuit military officers each drove them forward; ineffective urging could be impeached by the local governor-general or governor. At the Jingkou–Guazhou crossing on the Yangtze, the Zhenjiang circuit intendant was to lead civil and military officials in urging boats forward, and the regional commander was to patrol the riverbank and assist the crossing. When the regional commander post was abolished, a brigade commander took charge. In Yongzheng 3 grain-transport censor Zhang Tanlin memorialized on northern transport: first, from Tongzhou to Tianjin old station sectors were widely spaced; he asked that, following the five-li low-water spacing, officials who sat idle while boats were blocked and failed to report be impeached for ineffective urging; second, about thirteen or fourteen shallow stretches along the route could not be covered by the grain office alone; he asked that station troops dredge them while funds and grain remained under the grain office. Approved. Grain-transport censor Yilazha memorialized against abuses in the Henan grain intendant's urging; Governor Yin Jishan also asked to abolish corrupt customary fees presented by prefectures and counties to exchange supervisors and escort officers. When empty tribute boats returned to a province before exchange opened, the provincial governor and grain intendant were responsible; after exchange and departure, the grain transport governor-general and route officials; after reaching Tianjin, the granary superintendent, grain office, Tianjin regional commander, and Tongzhou brigade commander were to inspect strictly. Violators were to be seized and punished.
28
四十八年，漕督毓奇言：「各省督押，惟山東糧道抵通，餘祗押抵淮安。 嗣後各省重運，俱令糧道督押本幫至臨清，出具糧米無虧印結，即行回任。 其自臨清抵通，概令山東糧道往來催趲。 山東運河，每年十一月朔煞壩挑淺。 開壩之日，以南省漕船行抵台庄為準。 微山等湖收蓄眾泉，為東省濟運水櫝，不許民間私截水源。 徬河遇春夏水微，務遵漕規啟閉。 漕船到徬，須上下會牌俱到，始行啟板。 如河水充足，相機啟閉，以速漕運，不得兩徬齊啟，過泄水勢。 其在江中偶遇大風，原可停泊守候，而催漕官吏惟知促迫，軍船冒險進行，恆有漂沒之虞。 回空之船，管運員及運丁等恆意存怠玩，或吝惜雇價，將熟習舟子遣散，留不諳駕馭之人，而押運員弁每先行回署，並不在船督率，往往有運船失風之事。 」上諭飭「沿途各員催趲，應察風色水勢，毋得過於急迫，至涉險失事，亦不得因此旨遂任意逗留，致逾定限」。 初，運河中銅鉛船及木排，往往肆意橫行，民船多畏而讓之。 糧船北上，亦為所阻。 至是令巡漕御史轉飭沿途文武員弁，將運漕船催趲先行，餘船尾隨，循次前進，恃強爭先、不遵約束者，罪之。
In the forty-eighth year Grain Transport Governor Yu Qi said: "Among provincial escorts, only the Shandong grain intendant reached Tongzhou; the rest escorted only to Huai'an. Henceforth in heavy transport from every province, grain intendants were to escort their convoys to Linqing, issue sealed certificates of no grain loss, and return. From Linqing to Tongzhou the Shandong grain intendant alone was to travel back and forth urging transport. On the Shandong canal the dam was closed and the channel dredged on the first day of the eleventh month each year. When the dam opened, southern tribute boats were to have reached Taizhuang. Weishan and other lakes stored many spring waters as Shandong's transport reservoir; private diversion of sources was forbidden. When the Pang River ran low in spring and summer, gates had to be opened and closed according to transport regulations. When tribute boats reached the Pang, tally boards from upstream and downstream both had to arrive before the sluice could open. If water was ample, gates might be opened and closed as needed to speed transport, but both Pang gates must not be opened together and waste the water's force. When boats on the river met sudden high winds they could anchor and wait, but transport officials knew only haste; military boats pressed forward at risk and were constantly in danger of sinking. On empty return boats, transport officers and boatmen were often negligent, or stinted on wages, dismissed skilled helmsmen and kept unskilled men; escort officers often returned to office first and did not lead from the boats, so boats were often lost in storms. The Emperor ordered: "Officials along the route must observe wind and water and must not press so urgently as to court disaster; yet they must not use this edict as pretext for arbitrary delay beyond fixed deadlines." At first copper-and-lead boats and timber rafts on the canal often sailed recklessly, and civilian boats mostly feared them and gave way. Northbound grain boats were also obstructed by them. Thereupon the grain-transport censor was ordered to instruct route officials to urge tribute boats forward first, with other boats following in order; those who bullied their way ahead in defiance of regulations were punishable.
29
領運員弁，各省糧船分幫，每幫以衛所千總一人或二人領運，武舉一人隨幫效力。 順治六年，奏定就漕運各衛中擇其才幹優長者授職千總，責其押運，量功升轉，掛欠者治罪追償。 其後裁衛所外委百總，改為隨幫官。 康熙五十一年，揀候選千總三十員，發南漕標效力，如有領運千總員缺，聽總漕委署押運，果能抵通全完，倉場總督咨送兵部，准其即用。 揀選武舉，候推守衛所千總有原補隨幫者，可在總署處呈明，遇缺准其頂補，三年無誤，以衛千總推用。 雍正二年，漕運總督張大有奏稱山東、河南輪運薊州、遵化、豐潤官兵米石，沿途管押及回空催趲，例責成押運通判，請添設薊糧千總二，更番領運，從之。 各衛既有千總領運，而漕臣每歲另委押運幫官，分為押重押空，一重運費二三千金，一空運費浮於千金，幫丁之脂膏竭，而浮收之弊日滋矣。 嘉慶十二年，諭漕督不得多派委員，並禁止運弁等收受餽贈。 十四年，巡漕御史又請大加減省。 自咸豐三年河運停歇，船隻無存，領運之名亦廢。
Transport-leader officers: provincial grain boats were divided into gangs; each gang was led by one or two garrison thousand-commanders, with one military licentiate serving with the gang. In Shunzhi 6 it was fixed that from grain-transport garrisons men of superior talent were appointed thousand-commanders to escort transport, promoted by merit, and punished and made to restitute if deficits were recorded. Later outside-assistant hundred-commander posts in the garrisons were abolished and replaced by gang-attendant officers. In Kangxi 51 thirty candidate thousand-commanders were sent to serve with the southern transport banner; when a transport-leader vacancy arose, the grand grain transport commissioner might appoint one to escort, and if he reached Tongzhou with the load intact, the granary governor-general could memorialize the Board of War for immediate appointment. Selected military licentiates awaiting garrison thousand-commander appointment who had originally served as gang attendants might declare this at headquarters and fill vacancies; after three years without error they could be promoted as garrison thousand-commanders. In Yongzheng 2 Grain Transport Governor-General Zhang Dayou memorialized that rotating transport of grain and stone for Jizhou, Zunhua, and Fengrun garrisons in Shandong and Henan, with route escort and empty-return urging, was by regulation the escorting assistant magistrate's duty; he asked to add two Jizhou grain thousand-commanders to lead transport in rotation. Approved. Although garrisons already had thousand-commanders leading transport, the grain commissioner every year additionally appointed gang escort officers for heavy load and empty return; heavy transport cost two or three thousand taels and empty more than a thousand, draining the boatmen dry while illicit surcharges multiplied. In Jiaqing 12 an edict forbade the grain transport governor from over-appointing commissioners and prohibited transport officers from accepting gifts. In the fourteenth year the grain-transport censor again requested major reductions. From Xianfeng 3, when canal transport ceased and no boats remained, the title of transport leader was also abolished.
30
巡漕御史本明官，順治初省。 雍正七年，以糧船過淮陋規甚多，並夾帶禁物，遣御史二，赴淮安專司稽察。 糧船抵通，亦御史二稽察之。 乾隆二年，設巡漕御史四：一駐淮安，巡察江南江口至山東交境； 一駐濟寧，巡察山東台庄至北直交境； 一駐天津，巡察至山東交境； 一駐通州，巡察至天津。 凡徵收漕糧，定限十月開倉，十二月兌畢。 惟山東臨清徬內之船，改於次年二月兌開，依限抵通，徬外之船，仍冬兌冬開。 乾隆間，令徬內徬外一律春兌春開，從漕督楊錫紱請也。 嘉慶四年，諭曰：「冬兌冬開，時期促迫。 嗣後東省漕糧，仍照舊例起徵，運赴水次，立春後兌竣開幫，翌年改為冬兌春開。 」十五年，令徬河內外幫船，照春兌春開例辦理。 江北冬漕，定於十二月朔開兌，限次年二月兌竣開行。
The grain-transport censor was originally a Ming office, abolished at the beginning of Shunzhi. In Yongzheng 7, because many corrupt customs attended grain boats crossing the Huai and contraband was smuggled aboard, two censors were sent to Huai'an to inspect exclusively. When grain boats reached Tongzhou, two censors also inspected them. In Qianlong 2 four grain-transport censors were established: one at Huai'an, inspecting from the Jiangnan river mouth to the Shandong border; one at Jining, inspecting from Shandong's Taizhuang to the metropolitan border; one at Tianjin, inspecting to the Shandong border; one at Tongzhou, inspecting to Tianjin. Tribute grain collection was fixed to open granaries in the tenth month and finish exchange by the twelfth month. Only Shandong boats within the Pang at Linqing were changed to exchange and depart in the second month of the following year and reach Tongzhou by deadline; boats outside the Pang still exchanged and departed in winter. In the Qianlong reign boats inside and outside the Pang were ordered alike to exchange and depart in spring, at Grain Transport Governor Yang Xifu's request. In Jiaqing 4 an edict said: "Winter exchange and winter departure make the season too cramped. Henceforth Shandong tribute grain was again to be levied under the old rule, transported to the landing, exchanged and convoys opened after Beginning of Spring; the following year this became winter exchange and spring departure." In the fifteenth year convoy boats inside and outside the Pang were ordered handled under spring exchange and spring departure. Northern Jiangsu winter transport opened exchange on the first day of the twelfth month, with exchange finished and convoys opened by the second month of the following year.
31
凡漕兌，首重米色。 如有倉蠹作奸，攙和滋弊，及潮濕霉變，未受兌前，責成州縣，既受兌後，責在弁軍，覈驗之責，監兌官任之。 如縣衛因米色爭持，即將現兌米面同封固，送總漕巡撫查驗，果系潮濕攙雜，都令賠換篩颺，乃將米樣封送總漕，俟過淮後，盤查比較，分別糾劾。 然運軍勒索州縣，即借米色為由。 州縣開倉旬日，米多廒少，勢須先兌。 運軍逐船挑剔，不肯受兌，致糧戶無廒輸納，因之滋事。 運軍乘機恣索，或所索未遂，船竟開行，累州縣以隨幫交兌之苦。 及漕米兌竣，運弁應給通關。 通關出自尖丁。 尖丁者，積年辦事運丁也，他運丁及運弁皆聽其指揮。 尖丁索費州縣，不遂其欲，則靳通關不與，使州縣枉罹遲延處分。 運軍運弁沆瀣一氣，州縣惟恐誤兌，勢不得不浮收勒折以供其求。 上官雖明知其弊，而憚於改作。 且慮運軍裁革，遺誤漕運，於是含容隱忍，莫之禁詰。 州縣既多浮收，則米色難於精擇。 運軍既有貼費，受兌亦不復深求。 及至通州，賄賣倉書經紀，通挪交卸，米色潮濕不純之弊，率由於此。 積重難返，而漕政日壞矣。 乾隆間，漕運總督顧琮條上籌辦漕運七事：一，州縣親收漕糧，以免役胥藉端累民； 一，杜匿富僉貧包丁代運之弊； 一，受未開之幫船催令速行； 一，糧船過淮後，分員催趲，以速運漕； 一，河道舊有橫淺，豫為疏濬，以免阻滯； 一，各閘俱照漕規，隨時啟閉，江、廣漕船攜帶竹木，限地解卸； 一，回空三升五合餘米，速給副丁，以濟回時食用。 詔從其議。
In all grain exchange, grain color came first. If granary clerks committed fraud, adulteration bred abuses, or grain turned damp and moldy, before acceptance prefectures and counties were responsible; after acceptance officers and troops; verification lay with the exchange supervisor. If county and garrison disputed grain color, the grain being exchanged was sealed and sent to the grand grain transport commissioner and governor; if damp or adulterated, all were ordered to replace and winnow it, samples were sealed and sent to the grand grain transport commissioner, and after crossing the Huai they were compared and offenders impeached. Yet transport troops extorted prefectures and counties, using grain color as pretext. When prefectures and counties opened granaries for ten days, grain outnumbered granary space and exchange had to begin immediately. Transport troops picked faults boat by boat and refused acceptance, so grain households had no granary for delivery and disturbances followed. Transport troops seized the chance to demand freely; if demands were not met, boats simply departed, burdening prefectures and counties with catching up convoy by convoy. After tribute grain was fully exchanged, transport officers were to issue passage clearance. Passage clearance came from the lead boatman. The lead boatman was the transport boatman who had handled affairs for years; other boatmen and transport officers all obeyed him. Lead boatmen demanded fees from prefectures and counties; if refused, they withheld passage clearance and caused prefectures and counties to suffer delay penalties. Transport troops and officers acted in concert; prefectures and counties, fearing missed exchange, had no choice but to levy surcharges and squeeze deductions to meet their demands. Superiors knew the abuse well yet shrank from reform. They also feared that cutting transport troops would disrupt grain transport; so they tolerated and concealed it and none forbade or investigated. Once prefectures and counties levied many surcharges, grain color was hard to select carefully. Once transport troops had been paid supplementary fees, they no longer examined acceptance closely. By Tongzhou, bribing granary clerks and brokers to shift delivery, damp and impure grain mostly arose from this. Abuses piled up beyond reversal, and grain transport governance worsened daily. During the Qianlong reign Grain Transport Governor-General Gu Cong submitted seven proposals: first, prefectures and counties should collect tribute grain in person, lest clerks and runners burden the people; second, stop the rich hiding behind the poor, contracting boat quotas, and substituting transport; third, urge convoys not yet opened to depart quickly; fourth, after grain boats crossed the Huai, assign officers to urge them forward and speed transport; fifth, dredge old cross-channel shallows in advance to avoid blockage; sixth, all locks should open and close according to transport regulations; Jiang and Guangxi boats carrying bamboo and timber must unload at designated places; seventh, quickly give the three sheng five he of surplus grain from empty return to assistant boatmen for food on the return journey. An edict approved his proposals.
32
各省漕糧過淮，順治初，定限江北各府州縣十二月以內，江南江寧、蘇、松等處限正月以內，江西、浙江限二月以內，山東、河南限正月侭數開行。 如過淮違誤，以違限時日之多寡，定督撫糧道監兌推官降罰處分。 領運等官，捆打革職，帶罪督押。 其到通例限，山東、河南限三月朔，江北四月朔，江南五月朔，江西、浙江、湖廣六月朔。 各省糧船抵通，均限三月內完糧，十日內回空。 倉場定立限單，責成押幫官依限到淮，逾限不能到次，照章糾劾。
For tribute grain from every province crossing the Huai, at the beginning of Shunzhi the deadline was within the twelfth month for prefectures north of the Yangtze, within the first month for Jiangning, Suzhou, and Songjiang in Jiangnan, within the second month for Jiangxi and Zhejiang, and for Shandong and Henan to depart in the first month as early as possible. If crossing the Huai was delayed, governor-generals, governors, grain intendants, exchange supervisors, and pushing officials were demoted or penalized according to days exceeded. Transport-leader officers and the like were beaten, dismissed, and ordered to escort transport while under sentence. The deadline for reaching Tongzhou was the first day of the third month for Shandong and Henan, the fourth month for the north of the Yangtze, the fifth month for Jiangnan, and the sixth month for Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Huguang. Grain boats from every province reaching Tongzhou were alike limited to completing delivery within three months and returning empty within ten days. The granary office established deadline slips and held gang escort officers responsible for reaching the Huai on time; exceeding the deadline and failing to reach station brought impeachment under regulations.
33
承平日久，漕弊日滋。 東南辦漕之民，苦於運弁旗丁，肌髓已盡，控告無門，而運弁旗丁亦有所迫而然。 如漕船到通，倉院、糧廳、戶部雲南司等處投文，每船需費十金，由保家包送，保家另索三金。 又有走部，代之聚斂。 至於過壩，則有委員舊規，伍長常例，上斛下盪等費，每船又須十餘金。 交倉，則有倉官常例，並收糧衙署官辦書吏種種需索，又費數十金。 此抵通之苦也。 逮漕船過淮，又有積歇攤派吏書陋規，投文過堂種種費用。 總計每幫漕須費五六百金或千金不等。 此過淮之苦也。 從前運道深通，督漕諸臣只求重運如期抵通，一切不加苛察。 各丁於開運時多帶南物，至通售賣，藉博微利。 乾隆五十年後，黃河屢經開灌，運道日淤，漕臣慮船重難行，嚴禁運丁多帶貨物，於是各丁謀生之計絀矣。 運道既淺，反增添夫撥淺之費，每過緊要閘壩，牽挽動須數百人，道路既長，限期復迫，丁力之敝，實由於此。 雖經督撫大吏悉心調劑，無如積弊已深，迄未能收實效也。
After long peace, transport abuses grew daily. The people who managed transport in the southeast were exhausted by transport officers and banner boatmen until nothing remained and they had no recourse; yet transport officers and banner boatmen were also driven to it by pressure. When tribute boats reached Tongzhou, submitting documents at the granary superintendent's office, grain office, and Yunnan Bureau of the Board of Revenue cost ten taels per boat through guarantor households; guarantors charged an additional three taels. Runners also went about collecting fees in their stead. At each sluice dam came the commissioners' customary fees, the squad leaders' regular charges, and costs for measuring grain and cleaning holds—another ten-odd taels per ship. At granary delivery came the granary officers' customary fees plus endless demands from receiving-office clerks and yamen scribes—dozens of taels more. Such was the suffering of arrival at Tongzhou. Once the grain fleet crossed the Huai, entrenched surcharges fell on clerks and scribes, with fees for filing papers, appearing in court, and much else besides. Altogether each convoy cost five or six hundred taels, and in some cases as much as a thousand. Such was the suffering of the Huai crossing. In earlier times the canal ran deep and clear; grain supervisors cared only that the heavy haul reach Tongzhou on time, and imposed no extra scrutiny. At sailing season each transport soldier loaded southern goods, sold them at Tongzhou, and eked out a modest profit. After Qianlong 50 the Yellow River was repeatedly diverted for irrigation, the route silted ever shallower, and grain officials—fearing overloaded hulls—banned extra cargo. The transport soldiers' livelihood dwindled accordingly. Shallower waters meant new fees for lightening and hauling; at every critical lock and dam several hundred men might be needed to tow. Long distances and tight deadlines wore the transport soldiers down. Governors-general and governors labored to remedy the situation, but the abuses ran too deep and no lasting improvement followed.
34
各省漕船，原數萬四百五十五號。 嘉慶十四年，除改折分帶、坍荒裁減，實存六千二百四十二艘。 每屆修造十一，謂之歲造，其升科積缺漂沒者，謂之補修改造，限以十年。 至給價之多寡，視時之久暫、地之遠近為等差。 造船之費，初於民地徵十之七，軍地徵十之三，備給料價。 不足，則徵軍衛丁田以貼造漕船。 十年限滿，由總漕親驗，實系不堪出運，方得改造，有可加修再運者，量給加修銀，仍令再運。 按年計算，舊船可用，不驗明駕運，督撫查實糾劾。 司修造漕船各官，或詐朽壞，或修造未竣詐稱已完，或將朽壞船冊報掩飾，或承造推諉不依限竣工，或該管官督催不力，及朽壞船不估價申報，均降罰有差。
The provincial grain fleets originally totaled 10,455 vessels. By Jiaqing 14, after deductions for cash commutation, split conveyance, and cuts for ruined or abandoned land, 6,242 ships actually remained. Each year one-eleventh of the fleet was rebuilt—the so-called annual new build; ships lost to higher assessments, accumulated vacancies, or sinking were rebuilt under a supplemental ten-year schedule. Payments differed according to how long a ship had served and how far its home station lay. Building costs were first assessed at seven-tenths on civilian holdings and three-tenths on military land, to cover materials. When that fell short, garrison soldiers' fields were taxed to make up the cost of new grain ships. At the ten-year mark the Director-General of Grain Transport inspected in person; only ships truly unfit for duty could be rebuilt. Those fit for repair received proportional funds and were sent out again. By annual reckoning, any usable old ship put to sea without inspection would, once verified, bring impeachment upon the responsible governor. Officials overseeing grain-ship construction who feigned rot, declared work finished prematurely, hid decay in the registers, missed deadlines through evasion, supervised slackly, or failed to report decay for appraisal—all were demoted or punished in proportion.
35
直隸、山東、鳳陽地不產木，於清江關設廠，由船政同知督造。 江寧各幫共船千二百餘，亦於清江成造。 自儀徵逆流抵淮，四百餘里，沿途需用人夫挽曳，船成後復渡大江，道經千里，到次遲延，縣官急於考成，旗丁利於詐索，船未到即行交兌，名曰轉廒，於是贈耗、使費、賠補、苛索諸弊日滋，運軍苦之。 嗣裁船政同知，統歸糧道管理，令運軍支領料價赴廠成造，不敷，即於道庫減存漕項銀內動支。 徐州衛、河南後幫漕船，向亦在清江船廠成造，駕赴河南水次兌糧，程途遼遠，易誤兌限。 尋改在山東臨清設廠成造。 遇滿號之年，令各軍於江、安道庫銀內領價成造。 其濟南前幫，則在江南夏成鎮成造，嗣又改於臨清胡家灣設廠。
Because Zhili, Shandong, and Fengyang lacked timber, shipyards were established at Qingjiang Pass under an assistant prefect for ship administration. Jiangning's fleets—more than 1,200 ships in all—were likewise built at Qingjiang. From Yizheng upriver to the Huai was four hundred-odd li of towing; then the new hulls crossed the Yangtze and sailed a thousand li more, often arriving late. Magistrates rushed to meet their quotas; banner soldiers extorted what they could. Ships were turned over before they reached port—the so-called granary transfer—and gifts, wastage fees, indemnities, and squeeze grew worse by the day. The ship-administration post was later abolished and the yards placed under the grain-route intendant. Transport soldiers drew building funds at the yard; shortfalls came from grain-route silver held in treasury. Xuzhou Garrison and Henan rear-fleet ships had also been built at Qingjiang and sailed to Henan to take on grain—a journey so long that exchange deadlines were often missed. They were then assigned to new yards at Linqing in Shandong. In full-build years each garrison drew funds from the Jiangning and Anhui grain-route treasuries to construct its ships. The Jinan forward fleet was built at Xiacheng in Jiangnan, then moved to Hujiawan near Linqing.
36
船成查驗之法九：一驗木，二驗板，三驗底，四驗樑，五驗棧，六驗釘，七驗縫，八驗艙，九艙頭梢。 山東各幫於額運漕船外，向設量存船三十。 江蘇揚州亦有量存船二十四。 先後議裁，並將揚州衛應裁之船，抵補江、興二衛貧疲軍船。 乾隆八年，漕運總督顧琮上漕船變通事宜：一，漕船當大造之年，遇有減歇，即停造一年，與先運之船年限參差，將來無須同時配造； 一，賠造之船已出運多次，恆欠堅固，嗣後將賠造接算原船，已滿十年尚能出運者，准其將船在通售賣； 一，滿號之船，向俱分年抽造，其中堅固者，交總漕擇令加修，出運一次，許其流通變賣。 從之。 二十九年，漕督楊錫紱言：「各省漕船當十運屆滿應行成造之年，如運糧抵通，准在通變價。 再買補之船未經滿運，或中途猝遇風火，請准就地折變。 」詔從其議。 大河、淮安等幫漕船，恆有遭風沈溺之事。 阿桂奏稱，因船過高大，掉挽維艱所致，請較原定尺寸酌量減小。 嘉慶十五年，復酌減江、廣兩省漕船尺寸。 運丁利於攬載客貨，船身務為廣大，不知載重則行遲，行遲則壅塞，民船被阻，甚有相去數丈守候經旬者； 兼之強拏剝運，捶撻交加，怨聲載道，不僅失風之虞也。 十七年，以浙省成造漕船賠累日甚，每船除例給二百八兩外，復給銀五百九十餘兩，以紓丁力。 漕船建造修葺，其費有經常，有額外，年糜國帑數十百萬。 及其出運，勒索於州縣者又數十百萬。 催趲迎提，終歲勞攘，夾帶愈多，雖蘇、松內河，亦無歲不剝運。 剝運仍責舟於沿途，甚至攔江索費，奪船毀器，患苦商民，抗違官長，以天庾為口實，援漕督為護符，文武吏士，畏其勢焰，莫或究詰。
Completed ships were inspected on nine points: timber, planking, bottom, beams, decking, nails, seams, hold, and bow and stern cabins. Shandong's fleets kept thirty reserve ships beyond the quota fleet. Jiangsu's Yangzhou garrison likewise kept twenty-four reserve ships. After successive cuts, Yangzhou's decommissioned ships were reassigned to shore up the worn-out fleets of Jiangning and Xinghua garrisons. In Qianlong 8, Director-General Gu Cong proposed reforms: when a major build year coincided with reduced sailings, construction should pause for a year so active ships would age on staggered schedules and not all require rebuilding together. Second, indemnity-built ships, having sailed repeatedly, were seldom sturdy; henceforth they would count toward the original hull's term, and after ten years if still seaworthy they could be sold at Tongzhou. Third, ships at full term had been rebuilt in rotation; sturdy ones selected by the Director-General for one more repaired voyage might then be sold freely. The emperor assented. In year 29, Director Yang Xifu memorialized: "When a provincial grain ship completes ten voyages and reaches its rebuild year, if the grain has already reached Tongzhou, the hull may be sold there. Replacement ships not yet at full term, or those lost suddenly to wind or fire, should likewise be allowed to be commuted on the spot." The emperor approved. Ships of the Dahe, Huai'an, and other fleets were often lost in storms. A Gui reported that the hulls were too high and hard to tow, and asked that the standard dimensions be reduced. In Jiaqing 15 the grain ships of Jiangsu and Guangdong were again scaled down. Transport soldiers profited from passenger and freight traffic and built ever wider hulls, not grasping that heavier loads meant slower progress, slower progress meant jams, and civilian craft might wait ten days or more, several zhang apart. They also forced lighterage and beat those who resisted until outrage filled the roads—far beyond the mere danger of wind and capsizing. In year 17, Zhejiang's shipbuilding costs had grown crushing; beyond the statutory 280 taels each ship received another 590-odd taels to ease the transport soldiers' burden. Building and repairing grain ships cost millions from the treasury every year, both routine and extraordinary. Once at sea they extorted millions more from prefectures and counties. Hurried and met at every stage, they toiled year-round; smuggling only grew—and even on Suzhou and Songjiang's inner waterways lighterage was extracted every year. Lighterage still fell on civilian craft along the route; some blocked the river for fees, seized boats and smashed equipment, tormented merchants, and defied magistrates—using the imperial granary as excuse and the grain director as patron—while officials feared their clout and dared not inquire.
37
凡漕船載米，毋得過五百石。 正耗米外，例帶土宜六十石，雍正七年，加增四十，共為百石，永著為例。 旋准各船頭工舵工人帶土宜三石，水手每船帶土宜二十石。 嘉慶四年，定每船多帶土宜二十四石。 屯軍領運漕糧，冬出冬歸，備極勞苦，日用亦倍蓰家居，於是有夾帶私貨之弊。 漕船到水次，即有牙儈關說，引載客貨，又於城市貨物輻輳之處，逗留遲延，冀多攬載，以博微利。 運官利其餽獻，奸商竄入糧船，藉免國課。 其始運道通順，督漕諸臣不事苛察。 逮黃屢倒灌，運道淤淺，漕臣嚴申夾帶之禁，丁力益困。
No grain ship might carry more than 500 shi of grain. Beyond regular and wastage grain, statute allowed 60 shi of local goods; in Yongzheng 7 another 40 shi were added, fixed at 100 shi thereafter. Soon each ship's headmen, helmsmen, and crew were allowed three shi of local goods, and sailors twenty shi per ship. In Jiaqing 4 each ship was allowed twenty-four shi more of local goods. Garrison soldiers on grain duty sailed out in winter and home in winter, bearing extreme hardship at several times the cost of home life—hence the smuggling of private cargo. At landings brokers at once pressed them to take freight; in busy markets they lingered, hoping for more cargo and a little profit. Transport officials profited from their gifts, and merchants hid aboard grain ships to dodge state levies. At first the route ran clear and grain supervisors did not pry. When the Yellow River repeatedly flooded back and the channel shoaled, grain officials tightened the smuggling ban and the transport soldiers' plight worsened.
38
當商力充裕時，軍船回空過淮，往往私帶鹽斤。 漕運總督張大有條上六事：一，長蘆、兩淮產鹽之處，奸民勾串灶丁，私賣私販，伺回空糧船經過，即運載船中，請嚴行禁止，違者俱依私鹽例治罪； 一，糧船回空時，請於瓜洲、江口派瓜洲營協同廳員搜查； 一，運司等官拏獲私鹽，請依專管兼轄官例議敘； 一，隨幫官專司回空，有能拏獲私鹽三次及幫船三次回空無私鹽事者，以千總推用； 一，每船量帶食鹽四十斤，多帶者以私鹽例治罪； 一，例帶土宜之外，包攬商船木筏者，照漏稅例治罪，貨物入官。 自是禁網益密矣。 幫丁困苦，爰有津貼之議。 江蘇漕船，以松江幫丁力為最疲。 定例松、太等屬每船津貼銀三百兩，旋加為五百兩。 幫丁視為額給之項，仍欲另議津貼，開船遲延，州縣恐貽誤獲譴，恆私餽之，以致津貼日增，流弊無已。
In flush times, empty grain ships returning across the Huai often carried smuggled salt. Director-General Zhang Dayou proposed six measures: first, at Changlu and the Two Huai salterns, smugglers colluded with saltern workers and loaded salt onto returning empty grain ships—this should be strictly forbidden and punished under the private-salt law. Second, empty returning grain ships should be searched at Guazhou and Jiangkou with garrison officers assisting. Third, transport intendants who seized private salt should be rewarded under the dedicated-and-concurrent jurisdiction rules. Fourth, escort officers who seized private salt three times, or whose convoys returned empty three times without salt, should be promoted to company commander. Fifth, each ship might carry forty jin of table salt; more would be punished as private salt. Sixth, beyond statutory local goods, contracting to carry merchant vessels or rafts would be punished as tax evasion and the cargo confiscated. Thereafter the prohibition tightened. The transport soldiers' distress led to talk of subsidies. Of Jiangsu's grain fleets, Songjiang's transport soldiers were the most worn out. Statute set 300 taels of subsidy per ship for Songjiang, Taicang, and related districts; this was soon raised to 500. Transport soldiers treated the sum as fixed yet still demanded more, delaying sailings; magistrates, fearing punishment for late grain, paid them privately—so subsidies rose without end.
39
漕運抵通及遇淺，皆須用剝船。 清初設紅剝船六百艘，每船給田四十頃，收租贍船，免其徵科。 近畿州縣距河甚遠，恆雇覓民船，河干遊民藉之邀利，及接運漕糧，往往有盜賣攙和之弊，甚有盜賣將盡，故傾覆其船，逮運官查明，仍責地戶賠償，傾家盪業。 又領船船戶例受天津鈔關部差管轄，每歲河冰未泮之日，部差催促過堂守候，莫不有費，苦累實甚。 三十九年，裁紅剝船，依原收租數分派各省，於漕糧項下編徵，解糧道庫支發。 乾隆二年，定每船給紅剝銀二兩，由隨幫千總領發，漕船遇淺，由運軍自雇民船，坐糧廳酌定雇價。 十三年，增設★船六十艘，造船及用具夫役工食，均於紅剝銀內支用，餘仍分給運軍。 南糧入北河後，官為雇船剝運，糧艘未到，剝船先期預備，守候累日，且有妨商鹽挽運。 五十年，諭令另造剝船，南糧抵北河，即剝運赴通，嗣後毋得封固民船，致滋擾累，違者罪之。 尋議定官備剝船千二百艘，發交附近沿河天津等十八州縣收管，如有商貨鹽斤，許其攬載，四月以後，調赴水次，毋得遠離。 翌年復添造三百隻，交江西、湖廣成造，運送天津，與原設剝船在楊村更番備剝。 豫、東二省，因水淺阻滯，定造剝船三百艘，交德州、恩、武城、夏津、臨清五州縣分管。
Grain reaching Tongzhou and shallow stretches alike required lighter boats. Early in the dynasty 600 red lighter boats were established, each granted forty qing of land whose rent maintained the craft tax-free. Nearby counties lay far from the river and hired civilian boats; riverbank idlers profited. Grain handoffs often saw theft, sale, and adulteration; some sold nearly everything and then scuttled the boat—when officials traced the loss, the registered household still paid, ruining families. Registered boat households fell under Tianjin customs runners from the ministry; each spring before the ice broke, runners drove them to court and kept them waiting—all at their expense. In year 39 the red lighters were abolished; their former rents were reassessed among the provinces on grain quotas, paid into the grain-route treasury, and disbursed. In Qianlong 2 each ship received two taels of red-lighter silver from the convoy commander; in shoals transport soldiers hired civilian boats at rates set by the Grain Distribution Office. In year 13 sixty Fa lighter boats were added; building costs, gear, labor, and rations came from red-lighter funds, with the balance still paid to transport soldiers. After southern grain entered the northern canal, officials hired lighters; boats waited days before the grain arrived, sometimes many days, and merchant salt traffic suffered. In year 50 an edict ordered dedicated lighters; southern grain reaching the northern canal was to be lightered straight to Tongzhou. Civilian boats were no longer to be sealed and impressed, on pain of punishment. Official lighters were then fixed at 1,200, assigned to eighteen river counties near Tianjin; they might carry merchant freight or salt, and after the fourth month were posted to landings and kept close. The next year 300 more were built in Jiangxi and Huguang, sent to Tianjin, and rotated with the existing lighters at Yangcun. Henan and Shandong, where shoals caused delays, received 300 lighters managed by Dezhou, En, Wucheng, Xiajin, and Linqing.
40
清初沿明衛所之制，以屯田給軍分佃，罷其雜徭。 尋改衛軍為屯丁，毋得竄入民籍，五年一編審，糧道掌之。 康熙初，定各省衛所額設運丁十名。 三十五年，定漕船出運，每船僉丁一名，餘九名以諳練駕馭之水手充之。 凡僉選運丁，僉責在糧道，舉報責衛守備，用舍責運弁，保結責通幫各丁。 尋僉本軍子弟一人為副軍。 雍正初，免文學生員僉運。 先是江蘇按察使胡文伯以江、安十衛去蘇、松水次遙遠，遇有應更換之丁，運官赴衛查僉，往返須時，請預僉備丁，造冊送糧道，轉送總漕備案。 經戶部議准。 漕督楊錫紱上疏爭之，略言：「預僉閒丁，其不必者有二，不便者有二。 各省衛幫，貧富不等。 殷富之幫，本無俟閒丁預備； 貧乏之幫，遇有應換之丁，百計搜查，求一二殷丁且不可得，安有數十閒丁可以預備？ 其不必一也。 又殷實軍丁，生計粗裕，猝遇收成歉薄，一二年或即轉為貧乏，今既僉選註冊矣，設需用之時，已經貧乏，是仍以疲丁應選，其不必二也。 至送糧道點驗，僕僕道途，廢時失業，不便一也。 衛所州縣書吏，喜於有事，富者賄脫，貧者受僉，不便二也。 請停止預選閒丁註冊。 」從之。
Early in the Qing, following Ming guard-and-battalion practice, garrison land was allotted to soldiers for farming and miscellaneous corvée was lifted. Garrison soldiers were then renamed garrison colonists, barred from civilian registration; every five years the grain-route intendant conducted a household review. At the start of Kangxi each provincial guard was fixed at ten transport soldiers by quota. In year 35 one transport soldier was assigned per grain ship; the other nine posts went to skilled sailors. Selecting transport soldiers: the grain-route intendant chose them, the garrison commandant nominated them, transport officers appointed or dismissed them, and convoy soldiers stood surety. One garrison soldier was then chosen as deputy. At the start of Yongzheng, holders of literary degrees were exempt from transport duty. Earlier, Surveillance Commissioner Hu Wenbo of Jiangsu noted that Jiangning and Anhui's ten garrisons lay far from Suzhou and Songjiang landings; replacing transport soldiers required officers to travel to the garrison and back, and he asked to pre-select reserves, register them with the grain-route intendant, and file with the Director-General. The Ministry of Revenue approved. Director Yang Xifu objected in memorial, arguing in brief: "Pre-selecting idle soldiers is unnecessary on two counts and inconvenient on two. Provincial garrisons differed in wealth. Wealthy fleets had no need of idle reserves. Poor fleets, when a man had to be replaced, could scarcely find one or two solvent soldiers after every search—how could they keep dozens in reserve? That is the first needless point. Moreover, a solvent soldier might fall on one or two bad harvests and become poor; yet once registered, he would still be called up when already exhausted. That is the second needless point. Sending them to the grain-route intendant for inspection wastes time and livelihood on the road—the first inconvenience. Garrison and county clerks welcome any bustle; the rich bribe their way out and the poor get chosen—the second inconvenience. He requested that the advance selection and registration of standby transport hands be discontinued. The memorial was approved.
41
舊制漕船旗丁十名，丁地五頃。 其後丁地半歸民戶，運丁生計貧乏，經戶部行文清查，不許民間侵佔。 乾隆初，巡漕御史王興吾奏：「屯田籍冊年久散失，無可稽考。 亦有冊籍僅存而界址難於徵實，或軍丁典佃於民，而展轉相售、屢易其主者。 清田歸運，徒滋擾累。 蓋津貼之舉已成通例，民出費以贍丁，丁得項以承運，相沿既久，無礙於漕。 況丁得田不能自耕，勢必召佃收租，是與未贖時之津貼同一得項承運，未見有益也。 」二十五年，錫紱奏：「漕運之有疲幫，實緣運丁債負為累。 浙江之金、衢、嚴、溫、處、紹、台、嘉等幫，江南之江、淮、興、武、鳳陽、大河等幫，債欠尤多，幫疲益甚。 欲除私負之累，莫若出借官帑。 請於浙江江、安道庫各提銀六萬兩，專備疲幫領借。 每歲督運道員，查按沿途及抵通需用銀數，提交押運，至期散給，於次年新運應領項下扣還，俟疲幫漸起，奏明停止。
Under the old regulations, each grain-transport ship had a banner crew of ten men, with five qing of allotment land per sailor. Later, half of the sailors' allotment land passed into civilian hands. With transport crews left impoverished, the Board of Revenue ordered a full investigation and forbade further encroachment by civilians. Early in the Qianlong reign, grain-transport censor Wang Xingwu memorialized: "The registers of garrison-colony lands have been lost for years and can no longer be verified. Some registers still exist but boundaries can no longer be established; in other cases soldiers have leased their lands to civilians, and those plots have changed hands again and again in successive sales. Forcing cleared land back into transport service would only create fresh harassment and hardship. After all, the subsidy system had become standard practice: civilians paid to support the sailors, and the sailors used those funds to perform transport duty—an arrangement long in place that did not impede grain transport. Moreover, even if sailors regained the land, they could not farm it themselves and would have to lease it out for rent—so they would still rely on outside income for transport, just as under the subsidy system, with no real gain. In the twenty-fifth year, Yang Xifu memorialized: "The problem of exhausted transport fleets in the grain system stems chiefly from the debts weighing on transport sailors. Among the fleets of Jinhua, Quzhou, Yanzhou, Wenzhou, Chuzhou, Shaoxing, Taizhou, and Jiaxing in Zhejiang, and of Jiang, Huai, Xing, Wu, Fengyang, and Dahe in Jiangnan, debts were especially heavy and fleet exhaustion especially acute. To relieve them of private debt, the best course was to lend from the official treasury. He asked that sixty thousand taels be set aside from each of the Jiang and An circuit treasuries in Zhejiang, to be lent exclusively to exhausted fleets. Each year the supervising transport intendant would calculate the silver required along the route and at Tongzhou, submit the amount to the convoy officers, and disburse it on schedule; repayment would be deducted from the next year's transport allowances, and once exhausted fleets had recovered, he would memorialize to discontinue the lending program.
42
各省州縣衛幫承僉運丁，均以奉文派僉日起，限兩月僉解，並查明田地房產，造冊送總漕存案。 設有虧短掛欠，令其賠補。 若僉派後實系賣富差貧，或棄船脫逃，或重僉已革之丁，以及徇情出結、將軍丁改入民籍者，承僉之員降二級調用，不準抵銷。 其上司照失察例議處。 從漕督毓奇請也。 道光十三年，給事中金應麟奏：「江、浙內河一帶漕船，訛詐商民，有買渡、排幫等名目。 州縣以兌米畏其挑剔，置若罔聞，滯運擾民，為害甚大。 」詔林則徐、富呢揚阿嚴行查禁。
In every province, the officials responsible for levying transport sailors were required to complete the levy within two months of the dispatch order, investigate each man's fields and property, compile registers, and submit them to the Director-General of Grain Transport for the record. Any shortfall or deficit in grain delivery had to be made good by those responsible. If levies favored the wealthy while burdening the poor, if sailors abandoned their ships and fled, if dismissed men were re-levied, or if officials signed false certificates and reassigned military sailors to civilian registers, the levying officers were demoted two ranks and transferred, with no allowance for offsetting penalties. Their superiors were punished under the regulations for negligence. This was approved at the request of Grain Transport Governor Yu Qi. In the thirteenth year of the Daoguang reign, Supervising Secretary Jin Yinglin memorialized: "Along the inland waterways of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, grain-transport ships extort merchants under such headings as 'buying passage' and 'fleet blocking.' Prefectural and county officials, fearing harassment during grain loading, turned a blind eye—with the result that transport was delayed, the people were molested, and the harm was severe. An edict ordered Lin Zexu and Funiyang'a to investigate and strictly suppress the practice.
43
運軍往來淮、通，終歲勤苦，屯田所入有限，於是別給行月錢糧資用，其數各省不一。 江南運軍每名支行糧二石四斗至二石八斗，月糧八石至十二石。 浙江、江西、湖廣行糧三石，月糧九石六斗。 山東行糧二石四斗，月糧九石六斗。 其通、津等衛協運河南漕船運丁行月之數，與山東同。 各省領運千總等官，於廩俸外多有兼支行糧者。 行月二糧，舊時本少折多，且折價每石不過三四五錢，各處官丁常有偏枯之控。 詔令漕督議定查照歲支行月舊額本折各半，折色照漕欠每石銀一兩四錢，永著為令。 康熙二十九年，行月錢糧設立易知由單，列明應給各項錢糧，丁各一紙，照款支給。 如官役剋扣婪索，許本丁將事由載單內，於過淮時陳控。
Transport soldiers traveling between Huai'an and Tongzhou labored throughout the year, yet income from garrison-colony land was limited; they therefore received separate travel and monthly grain allowances for expenses, the amounts varying by province. In Jiangnan, each transport soldier received two shi four dou to two shi eight dou in travel grain and eight to twelve shi in monthly grain. In Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Huguang, travel grain was three shi and monthly grain nine shi six dou. In Shandong, travel grain was two shi four dou and monthly grain nine shi six dou. For transport sailors on Henan grain ships convoyed by guards at Tongzhou, Tianjin, and elsewhere, travel and monthly allowances matched those of Shandong.
