In every province, the lieutenants and other officers leading transport often drew travel grain in addition to their salary rations. Under the old system, travel and monthly allowances were largely paid in commuted cash rather than grain, and the commutation rate was no more than three to five qian per shi—leading to frequent complaints of unfair treatment from officers and sailors alike. An edict instructed the grain-transport governor to set fixed ratios: half the old annual travel and monthly allowance in kind, half in commuted cash at the standard grain deficit rate of one tael and four qian per shi—a rule thereafter permanently in force. In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi, an itemized payment voucher was introduced for travel and monthly allowances; each sailor received one, listing every amount due, and was paid accordingly. If officials or clerks withheld or extorted payments, the sailor could note the grievance on his voucher and file a complaint when passing Huai'an.
44
雍正元年，覆准運船到次，先將本色行月錢糧於三日內給發折色銀，由衛守備出具印領受，領運千總鈐章，解道驗明，以半給軍，半封固，糧道賚淮，由總漕監發，愆期遲延者罪之。 乾隆五年，議定運丁於解淮驗給一半錢糧內，酌留回空費用，數多者扣留三之一，少者酌扣八兩，令糧道另行封兌，於過淮時交隨運官弁收領，俟抵通交糧後，給發各丁。 緣各省漕船回空，每因資斧缺乏，不能及時抵次也。 十年，漕督顧琮上言：「糧道所押幫船，多少不同，兌開復有遲早，必俟最後之幫開竣，方得赴幫督察，而首進之幫，又不免守候領銀之累。 請仍令糧道兌准封給領運千總，解淮呈驗散給。 」從之。
In the first year of Yongzheng, it was approved that when transport ships arrived at their stations, commuted silver for travel and monthly allowances in kind must be issued within three days. The guard assistant commander would issue a stamped receipt, the leading transport lieutenant would affix his seal, and the payment would be submitted to the intendant for verification. Half was paid to the soldiers at once and half sealed for later delivery; the grain intendant carried the sealed portion to Huai'an, where the Director-General of Grain Transport supervised its disbursement. Officials who missed the deadline were punished. In the fifth year of Qianlong, it was decided that from the half of the allowance paid at Huai'an, a portion would be reserved for the return voyage—one-third when the total was large, or eight taels when it was small. The grain intendant sealed this separately and handed it to convoy officers at Huai'an; it was disbursed to each sailor only after the grain had been delivered at Tongzhou. This was because returning grain ships from every province often lacked funds for the voyage home and could not reach their stations on time. In the tenth year, Grain Transport Governor Gu Cong submitted: "The grain intendant escorts fleets of varying size, and loading schedules differ. He cannot inspect a fleet until the last convoy has finished loading, yet the first convoys to arrive are burdened with waiting to receive their silver payments. He asked that the grain intendant again be allowed to seal the verified payments and hand them to the leading transport lieutenant for presentation and disbursement at Huai'an. The request was approved.
45
凡漕船停歇，月糧減半給發，民船停運，給月糧原額四之一。 三十年，車駕南巡，截留江、浙二省冬兌漕糧各十萬石，減歇之船，於應給月糧外，加恩再給十之二，以示體恤。 運軍月糧，遇閏按月本折均平支給，尋罷。 嗣以閏月錢糧乃計日授食，各軍春出冬歸，停支一月，不免枵腹。 山東、河南、浙江、江寧、鳳陽等衛閏月有糧，仍照原額支給。 山東、浙江及蘇、太等衛，遇閏各有額編加徵銀，江、興等衛無之，遇閏於道庫減存銀內支用。 江西、湖北、湖南系按出運船米之數支給。 河南遇閏亦無加徵銀，向准山東等省一例支給，經部駁追，尋准其照支。
When grain-transport ships were idle, monthly grain was paid at half the usual rate; when civilian ships suspended service, one-quarter of the standard monthly allowance was paid. In the thirtieth year, during the southern tour, one hundred thousand shi of winter-exchange grain from each of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were retained; for ships idled as a result, an additional twenty percent beyond the usual monthly allowance was granted as an act of imperial consideration. Transport soldiers' monthly grain during intercalary months had been paid evenly between grain and commuted cash, but this practice was soon abolished. It was later argued that intercalary-month allowances were calculated as daily rations; since the soldiers departed in spring and returned in winter, withholding one month's grain left them hungry. For guards in Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, Jiangning, Fengyang, and elsewhere that received intercalary-month grain, the original allowance continued to be paid. In Shandong, Zhejiang, and guards such as Suzhou and Taicang, special silver levies were assessed in intercalary years; guards such as Jiang and Xing had none, and intercalary allowances there were paid from retained silver in the circuit treasury. In Jiangxi, Hubei, and Hunan, intercalary allowances were paid according to the volume of grain shipped. Henan had no special intercalary levy either; payment on the Shandong model was initially approved, then rejected and ordered recovered by the Board, but was later approved again.
46
各省運軍名數參差不齊。 江、浙每船十一二名不等。 嗣議定每船概以十軍配運，按名支給行月。 安慶衛舊系按漕用軍按名派行月二糧。 自畫一裁減後，每船祗用十軍，而所載漕糧則倍於他船，應仍按糧支給行月。 山東德州等衛有自雇民船裝運漕糧者，一體支給行月錢糧。 江寧省衛無贍運屯田，遇有減存，同出運之船支給安家月糧。 江淮、興武二衛，原
The number of transport soldiers varied from province to province. In Jiangsu and Zhejiang, each ship carried eleven or twelve men. It was later fixed that each ship would carry ten soldiers, with travel and monthly allowances paid to each by name. Anqing Guard had formerly allotted travel and monthly grain to each soldier engaged in grain transport. After the uniform reduction to ten soldiers per ship, Anqing ships still carried twice the grain of others, and travel and monthly allowances continued to be paid according to cargo volume. In Dezhou and other Shandong guards where civilian ships were hired to carry grain, travel and monthly allowances were paid on the same terms. Jiangning guards had no garrison land to support transport; when reductions occurred, they received settling-in monthly allowances along with ships going out on duty. For the Jianghuai and Xingwu guards, which had formerly
47
減駕軍二名，准其復設，派給行月二糧，例由布政司行文各府州縣支領，每船餽遺書吏六七金不等，否則派撥遠年難支錢糧及極遠州縣，而州縣糧書又有需索，每船約二三金不等。 十金之糧，運丁所得實不及半也。
had two helm soldiers eliminated but were permitted to restore them, with travel and monthly grain allotted accordingly. By regulation, the provincial administration commissioner ordered disbursement through the prefectures and counties—but each ship paid clerks six or seven taels in gifts, or else was assigned hard-to-collect arrears from distant counties, while county grain clerks exacted another two or three taels per ship. Of a ten-tael grain allowance, the transport sailor actually received less than half.
48
漕糧為天庾正供，司運官吏考成綦嚴。 順治十二年，定漕、糧二道考成則例。 經徵州縣衛所各官，漕糧逾期未完，分別罰俸、住俸、降級、革職，責令戴罪督催，完日開復。 康熙二年，議定隨漕行月、輕齎各項錢糧，總作十分計算，原參各官限一年接徵，而接徵之員止限半年，殊未平允。 嗣後接徵官限一年，糧道、知府、直隸州一年半，巡撫二年。 如仍不完，照原參分數議處。 其經徵督催白糧各官考成條例，悉與漕糧同。 白糧項下減存經費銀不得擅用，違者題參，並勒令賠繳。 糧道完儲錢糧，春秋造冊達部，候撥解京餉。 年終及離任日，籓司盤查出如有侵虧，揭報巡撫題參。
Grain transport supplied the imperial granaries, and officials responsible for transport were held to the strictest performance standards. In the twelfth year of Shunzhi, performance regulations were established for the grain-transport and grain-intendant circuits. Collecting officials at prefectures, counties, guards, and posts who failed to complete grain collection on time faced fines, salary suspension, demotion, or dismissal, and were ordered to supervise collection while under censure—restored only upon completion. In the second year of Kangxi, travel, monthly, and light-courier allowances were counted as ten parts in total; officials originally held responsible were given one year to collect arrears, but the officials actually doing the collecting had only half a year—a manifestly unfair arrangement. Thereafter, collecting officials were given one year, the grain intendant, prefect, and directly governed department one and a half years, and the governor-general two years. If collection remained incomplete, penalties were applied according to the original proportion reported. Performance regulations for officials collecting and supervising tribute rice were identical to those for grain transport. Retained operating funds under the tribute-rice account could not be used without authorization; violators were reported and ordered to repay in full. When the grain intendant completed stored allowances, registers were submitted to the Board in spring and autumn, pending allocation for capital disbursements. At year's end and upon leaving office, the provincial treasurer audited accounts; any embezzlement or deficit was reported to the governor-general for investigation.
49
凡漕欠，無論多寡，均發各糧道嚴追，承追官吏嚴查本弁本軍產業，估計變售償補。 如運軍侵糧逃逸，報明戶部，行文總督提究。 掛欠米石，追完補運，與本幫原欠米不符者，將過淮不駁換之總漕及督漕、承運各官並採買搭運之員，一併糾劾。 其運到之米，按數收用，以免累及運軍。 承平日久，法令日弛，糧道及監兌、押運官既不親臨水次，糧船抵淮，漕總復不嚴行稽查，於是弁軍任意折銀，沿途盜賣，抵關時遂多掛欠矣。
All grain-transport deficits, whatever their size, were assigned to the grain intendants for strict recovery; recovering officials were to identify the officers' and soldiers' property, sell it, and use the proceeds for compensation. If transport soldiers embezzled grain and fled, the matter was reported to the Board of Revenue and the governor-general was instructed to investigate and prosecute. When recovered grain used to make up a deficit did not match the fleet's original shortage, the Director-General who had approved passage at Huai'an without rejecting substitutions, together with grain-transport supervisors, convoy officers, and officials who purchased supplemental grain, were all impeached together. The grain that arrived was accepted in full so that transport soldiers would not be further penalized. After long years of peace, enforcement grew slack. Grain intendants and exchange and convoy officials no longer attended the landing in person, and when grain ships reached Huai'an the grain-transport director failed to inspect them strictly. Officers and soldiers then commuted allowances to silver at will, sold grain along the way, and by the time they reached the toll station many were reporting deficits.
50
四十五年，令嗣後耗贈漕截等銀米，暫存糧道倉庫，俟回空時，倉場查明，按其掛欠數扣抵。 不足，以行糧抵補。 旋議定掛欠漕糧不及一分至六分之弁軍治罪，總漕、糧道按所欠分數議處，並將所欠漕糧，由總漕、糧道及監兌、押運、僉丁、衛所各官至運丁，分別擔任，均限定期內償還。 不完，總漕、糧道交部議，運官、運軍分別治罪，仍責成總漕、糧道賠償。 全完者，優敘。
In the forty-fifth year, it was ordered that loss, gift, and grain-cut allowances in silver and grain be temporarily stored in the grain intendant's warehouse; upon the return voyage, the granary department would verify accounts and deduct any reported deficit from these reserves. If the reserves proved insufficient, travel grain was used to cover the shortfall. Regulations were soon set: officers and soldiers with grain deficits of one to six tenths faced punishment; the Director-General and grain intendant were dealt with according to the proportion owed; and responsibility for the deficit was assigned at every level—from the Director-General and grain intendant through exchange supervisors, convoy officers, levy officials, guard officers, and transport sailors—all required to repay within a fixed term. If repayment was not completed, the Director-General and grain intendant were referred to the Board for judgment; transport officers and soldiers were punished separately; and the Director-General and grain intendant remained liable for compensation. Those who made full repayment received preferential commendation.
51
糧船抵通起卸漕米，例買別幫餘米抵補。 雍正三年，奏准嗣後漕米如有不足，即分別參處償還，不得以別幫餘米買補。 其運軍日用餘米，許其售賣，餘並禁阻。
When grain ships reached Tongzhou to unload, shortfalls were customarily covered by purchasing surplus grain from other fleets. In the third year of Yongzheng, it was approved that any future shortfall in grain transport must be made good through individual investigation and repayment—purchase of surplus grain from other fleets would no longer be permitted. Transport soldiers were permitted to sell surplus grain for daily use; all other sales were forbidden.
52
漕船經涉江湖，偶遇風濤漂沒，沿途催趲各官，及汛地文武官，親臨勘驗出結，總漕及巡撫覆勘奏免。 若軍弁詐報漂沒，及漂沒而損失不多，乘機侵盜至六百石者，擬斬； 不及六百石，充發極邊，漕米按數賠繳。 文武官遇漕船沈溺，不將情由申報，押運官弁巡查不謹，致失火焚毀者，俱降一級調用。 地方官不協救，延燒他船者，罰俸一年。 雍正初，奏准漕船在內河失風漂沈者，不許豁免，押運官弁照失於防範例，罰俸一年。 如有假捏，嚴加治罪，出結官弁，從重議處。 凡海洋江河遭風漂沒，領運弁軍幸獲生全者，照軍功保守在事有功例，晉級賜金。 其漂沒身故者，官弁照軍功陣亡例，分別准廕加贈，運軍給予祭葬銀。
When grain ships crossing rivers and lakes were lost to wind and waves, route officials and garrison civil and military officers personally inspected and certified the loss; the Director-General and governor-general then re-inspected and memorialized for exemption from repayment. If officers or soldiers falsely reported a loss, or if the actual loss was small but they seized the opportunity to embezzle six hundred shi or more, the proposed sentence was decapitation; For amounts under six hundred shi, the sentence was penal servitude in the remotest frontier, with grain repaid in full. Civil and military officials who failed to report the circumstances when grain ships sank, and convoy officers whose negligent patrol allowed fires that destroyed ships, were all demoted one rank and transferred. Local officials who failed to assist in rescue and allowed fire to spread to other ships were fined one year's salary. In the early Yongzheng reign, it was approved that grain ships lost to wind and sinking on inland rivers would not be exempted from repayment; convoy officers were fined one year's salary under the regulations for failure of precaution. Fabricated reports were punished severely, and certifying officers were dealt with more harshly still. When wind or water caused loss on sea or river, leading transport officers and soldiers who survived were promoted and rewarded with gold under the regulations for military merit in holding one's post under fire. Those who died in such losses—officers received hereditary privileges and posthumous honors under the regulations for death in battle; transport soldiers received funeral and sacrificial silver.
53
乾隆七年，議定漕船失風火災，船未沉沒，無論已未過淮，即令修固復載抵通。 如已被沈難戽者，雇民船載運，隨幫過淮盤驗抵通。 如失事在過淮以後，黃河中流，民船難募，令先分通幫帶運開行，沿途仍雇覓民船裝載。 通幫各丁，出具互結，稍有虧欠，責令償補。 江、廣漕船失風沈溺，如果不堪戽修，無論已未滿號，地方官驗明，申報總漕，就近變價，令運弁賚交糧道發給。 回空漕船失事亦如之。 嗣議准江蘇、浙江、山東、河南等省買補船艘，如已滿號，遇失風事故，就近折變，價銀封交員弁攜回，由糧道驗給各軍，以補新漕。 漕船遇冰凌迅下，致被損壞，及雷火焚毀，沈失米糧，免其償補。
In the seventh year of Qianlong, it was decided that if a grain ship struck by wind or fire had not sunk, it must be repaired and reloaded for delivery at Tongzhou, whether or not it had yet passed Huai'an. If the ship had sunk and could not be bailed out, civilian vessels were hired to carry the grain, convoyed with the fleet past Huai'an for inspection and on to Tongzhou. If the accident occurred after passing Huai'an, in the middle reaches of the Yellow River where civilian vessels were hard to find, the grain was first divided among Tongzhou-bound fleets for convoy transport, while civilian ships were hired along the route to carry the rest. Each sailor in the Tongzhou fleet signed mutual guarantees; any shortfall had to be made good. When grain ships from Jiangxi and Huguang were lost to wind and sinking and could not be repaired, local officials verified the facts regardless of whether the ship had completed its quota, reported to the Director-General, sold the wreck locally, and had transport officers deliver the proceeds to the grain intendant for disbursement. Returning empty grain ships were handled the same way. It was later approved that Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shandong, Henan, and other provinces could purchase replacement ships; if a ship that had completed its quota was lost to wind, it was sold locally, the proceeds sealed and sent back by officers, verified and disbursed by the grain intendant to the soldiers for new grain transport. When grain ships were damaged by sudden ice floes or destroyed by lightning and fire, with grain sunk and lost, repayment was waived.
54
各省漕糧，歲有定額，凡荒地無徵者，督撫勘實報免，隨漕銀米，一例蠲免。 災傷之區，應徵漕糧，及折改漕價，酌量各被災輕重，分別緩徵、帶徵。 遇帶徵之年，復又被災傷，分年壓徵帶補。 沿江沿海田地坍沒水中者，保題豁免。 水旱偏災民地，例得蠲免，惟應船役，即被災甚重，仍須供修船雇募等事，不得同邀寬典。 康熙三十七年，議定京畿通州、武清、寶坻、香河、東安、永清六州縣紅剝船戶所領地，水旱一體蠲免。 水淹田畝，例於歲終確勘，涸前起徵，淹則停免。 雍正十年，定淹田漕米照壓徵例，俟冬勘後，涸則帶徵，淹則豁免。
Each province had a fixed annual grain quota; where land lay fallow and no tax was due, the governor-general verified and memorialized for exemption, and accompanying grain-transport silver and grain were exempted as well. In disaster-stricken areas, due grain and commuted grain payments were assessed according to the severity of damage, with collection deferred or carried forward as appropriate. If disaster struck again during a year of carried-forward collection, arrears were spread over successive years. Fields along rivers and coastlines that collapsed into the water were reported through guarantors for full exemption. Fields partially stricken by flood or drought were normally eligible for remission, but boat-service obligations—even in severe disaster—still required ship repair, hired recruitment, and the like, and could not claim the same relief. In Kangxi 37, allotments of red lighterage boat households in Tongzhou, Wuqing, Baodi, Xianghe, Dong'an, and Yongqing in the capital region were given unified remission in flood and drought alike. Flooded fields were surveyed at year's end by regulation; collection began when water receded and stopped while fields stayed submerged. In Yongzheng 10, flooded-field tribute grain followed deferred-collection precedent: after winter survey, collection resumed when dry and was exempted while flooded.
55
蘇、松、太三屬為東南財賦之區，賦額最重。 世宗以來，屢議蠲緩，然較之同省諸府縣，尚多四五倍或十數倍。 道光時，兩遭大水，各州縣每歲歉蠲減，遂成年例。 嗣是徵收之數，除官墊民欠，每年僅得正額之七八或五六而已。 軍興以後，兩府一州，受害尤酷。 同治二年，諭江督、蘇撫查明，折衷議減，期與舊額本輕之常、鎮二府，通融覈計，著為定額。 其紳戶把持、州縣浮收諸弊，永遠禁革。 四年，戶部遵議：「江蘇常、鎮、太五屬編徵米，系會同漕贈行月南恤局糧等款徵收。 應如李鴻章等所奏，無分起運留支，一體並減，酌科則之重輕，視減成之多寡，計原額編徵米豆二百二萬餘石，減五十四萬餘石。 」民困稍舒。 曾國籓又請將蘇、松地漕錢糧一體酌減。 部覆漕項為辦運要需，若議覈減，費必不敷，勢須另加津貼，於民生仍無裨益。 詔令國籓、鴻章仿浙省成例，覈實刪減浮收，並嚴禁大戶包攬短交等弊。 是年減浙江杭、嘉、湖三屬米二十六萬餘石。
Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang—the southeast's chief revenue region—bore the heaviest tax quotas. Since Yongzheng, remissions and deferrals were debated repeatedly, yet compared with other prefectures in the province they still ran four or five times higher, or even tenfold. In Daoguang, after two great floods, each prefecture and county received annual poor-harvest remissions until this became fixed practice. Thereafter, apart from official advances for unpaid civilian arrears, collections each year reached only seven or eight parts in ten of the regular quota, or even five or six. After military campaigns began, the two prefectures and one department suffered especially hard. In Tongzhi 2, the Jiangsu governor-general and governor were ordered to investigate, negotiate balanced reductions, and fix quotas by flexible calculation with Chang and Zhen, whose old quotas had been lighter. Abuses such as gentry control and excessive collection by prefectures and counties were permanently banned. In the fourth year, the Board approved: "Compiled tribute grain for Jiangsu's Chang, Zhen, and Taicang jurisdictions was collected with canal stipends, monthly southern relief grain, and the like. As Li Hongzhang memorialized, dispatched and retained grain alike should be reduced together; of the original 2.02 million-odd shi of compiled grain and beans, 540,000-odd shi were to be cut according to tax weight and reduction scale. Popular hardship eased somewhat. Zeng Guofan also requested balanced reduction of Suzhou and Songjiang land tribute and canal payments. The Board replied that canal funds were essential; reductions would leave expenses short and require extra subsidies, bringing no real benefit to the people. An edict ordered Guofan and Hongzhang to follow Zhejiang's precedent, cut verified excessive collection, and strictly forbid large households' monopolizing transport and short delivery. That year Hang, Jia, and Hu in Zhejiang reduced grain by more than 260,000 shi.
56
海運始於元代，至明永樂間，會通河成，乃罷之。 清沿明代長運之制。 嘉慶中，洪澤湖泄水過多，運河淺涸，令江、浙大吏兼籌海運。 兩江總督勒保等會奏不可行者十二事，略謂，「海運既興，河運仍不能廢，徒增海運之費。 且大洋中沙礁叢雜，險阻難行，天庾正供，非可嘗試於不測之地。 旗丁不諳海道，船戶又皆散漫無稽，設有延誤，關係匪細」。 上謂「海運既多窒礙，惟有謹守前人成法，將河道盡心修治，萬一嬴絀不齊，惟有起剝盤壩，或酌量截留，為暫時權宜之計，斷不可輕議更張，所謂利不百不變法也」。 自是終仁宗之世，無敢言海運者。
Sea transport began under the Yuan; in Ming Yongle, when the Tonghui Canal was completed, it was discontinued. The Qing followed the Ming long-distance canal transport system. In Jiaqing, because Hongze Lake discharged too much and the Grand Canal grew shallow, Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors were also ordered to plan sea transport. Governor-General Lebao and others listed twelve reasons sea transport would not work: "Once sea transport begins, canal transport still cannot be abandoned, yet sea costs are added for nothing. Moreover, sand reefs scatter across the open ocean and passage is perilous; the empire's regular grain supply cannot be tried in uncertain waters. Banner boatmen do not know sea routes; boat households are scattered and unregistered; any delay would have grave consequences. The emperor said sea transport had too many obstacles; only careful maintenance of predecessors' methods and devoted canal repair would do. If surplus and deficit failed to balance, transshipment at dams or measured diversion might serve as temporary expedient—but the system must not be lightly changed; benefit must be a hundredfold before law is changed. Thereafter, through Jiaqing's end, none dared speak of sea transport.
57
道光四年，南河黃水驟漲，高堰漫口，自高郵、寶應至清江浦，河道淺阻，輸輓維艱。 吏部尚書文孚等請引黃河入運，添築閘壩，鉗束盛漲，可無泛溢。 然黃水挾沙，日久淤墊，為患滋深。 上亦知借黃濟運非計，於是海運之議復興。 詔魏元煜、顏檢、張師誠、黃鴻傑各就轄境情形籌議。 諸臣憚於更張，以窒礙難行入奏。 會孫玉庭因渡黃艱滯，軍船四十幫，須盤壩接運，請帑至百二十萬金。 未幾，因水勢短絀，難於挽運，復請截留米一百萬石。 上令琦善往查，覆稱玉庭所奏渡黃之船，有一月後尚未開行者，有淤阻御黃各壩之間者，其應行剝運軍船，皆膠柱不能移動。 上震怒，元煜、玉庭、檢均得罪。
In Daoguang 4, Yellow River water at the Southern Rivers rose suddenly, the Gaoyan dam overflowed, and from Gaoyou and Baoying to Qingjiangpu the canal was shallow and transport painfully difficult. Board of Civil Appointments Minister Wen Fu and others requested diverting Yellow River water into the canal and adding sluices and dams to confine the flood. Yet Yellow River water carries silt; over time it silts and fills, and harm grows deeper. The emperor also knew borrowing the Yellow River to aid transport was no real plan, and debate over sea transport revived. An edict ordered Wei Yuanyu, Yan Jian, Zhang Shicheng, and Huang Hongjie each to plan according to conditions in their jurisdictions. The ministers, fearing change, reported that obstacles made implementation impossible. Then Sun Yuting, with Yellow River crossing obstructed, reported that forty gangs of military boats required transshipment at dams and requested 1.2 million taels from the treasury. Before long, with water insufficient and towing difficult, he again requested diversion of one million shi. The emperor ordered Qishan to investigate; his report said some listed Yellow River boats had not departed even a month later and some were stuck between silt-blocked dams; boats due for transshipment were frozen in place. The emperor was greatly angered; Yuanyu, Yuting, and Jian were all punished.
58
協辦大學士、戶部尚書英和建言：「治道久則窮，窮則必變。 河道既阻，重運中停，河漕不能兼顧，惟有暫停河運以治河，雇募海船以利運，雖一時之權宜，實目前之急務。 蓋滯漕全行盤壩剝運，則民力勞而帑費不省，暫雇海船分運，則民力逸而生氣益舒。 國家承平日久，航東吳至遼海者，往來無異內地。 今以商運決海運，則風颶不足疑，盜賊不足慮，霉濕侵耗不足患。 以商運代官運，則舟不待造，丁不待募，價不待籌。 至於屯軍之安置，倉胥之稽察，河務之張弛，胥存乎人。 矧借黃既病，盤壩亦病，不變通將何策之從？ 臣以為無如海運便。 」詔仍下有漕各省大吏議。 時琦善督兩江，陶澍撫安徽，咸請以蘇、松、常、鎮、太倉四府一州之粟全由海運。 乃使布政使賀長齡親赴海口，督同地方官吏，招徠商船，並籌議剝運兌裝等事。 嗣澍言：「現雇沙船千艘，三不像船數十，分兩次裝載，計可運米百五六十萬石。 其安徽、江西、湖廣離海口較遠，浙江乍浦、寧波海口或不能停泊，或盤剝費鉅，仍由河運。 」上乃命設海運總局於上海，並設局天津。 覆命理籓院尚書穆彰阿，會同倉場侍郎，駐津驗收監兌，以杜經紀人需索留難諸弊。
Associate Grand Secretary and Board of Revenue Minister Yinghe proposed: "Governance long continued reaches its limits; at its limits it must change. The canal is obstructed and major transport halted; canal tribute cannot be managed together—canal transport must be suspended temporarily to repair the river and hire sea boats to aid transport. Though expedient, it is the urgent task of the moment. If all stalled tribute is transshipped at dams, popular labor is exhausted yet treasury expense is not saved; if sea boats are hired for partial transport, labor is eased and hardship relieved. The state has enjoyed long peace; vessels from eastern Wu to the Liaohai pass like inland routes. If merchant transport decides sea transport, typhoons, bandits, and mold need not be feared. If merchant transport replaces official transport, boats need not be built, crews need not be recruited, and prices need not be raised. Settling garrison troops, auditing warehouse clerks, and tightening or loosening river affairs—all depend on men. Borrowing the Yellow River is harmful and transshipment at dams is harmful too; without change, what policy can be followed? Nothing is as convenient as sea transport, he argued. An edict again referred the matter to grain-transport provincial governors. Qishan governed the two Jiangs and Tao Shu Anhui; both requested that grain from Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Taicang go entirely by sea. Financial commissioner He Changling went in person to the port to supervise local officials in recruiting merchant boats and planning transshipment, exchange, and loading. Later Shu reported: "We have hired one thousand sand boats and several dozen 'three-unlike' boats in two batches, for 1.5 to 1.6 million shi. Anhui, Jiangxi, and Huguang are farther from the port; at Zhejiang's Zhabu and Ningbo ports boats cannot anchor or transshipment costs are enormous—they still go by canal. The emperor ordered a sea-transport general bureau at Shanghai and a bureau at Tianjin. Granary Superintendent Mu Zhang'a was sent with the capital granary superintendent to Tianjin to inspect and supervise exchange and stop brokers' demands and obstruction.
59
六年正月，各州縣剝運之米，以次抵上海受兌，分批開行。 計海運水程四千餘里，逾旬而至。 米石抵通後，轉運京倉，派步軍統領衙門文武員弁沿途稽查。 沙船耗米，於例給旗丁十八萬餘石內動放，所節省耗米六萬石，仍隨同起運。 承運漕糧每石給耗米八升，白糧耗米一斗，以補正米之不足。 仍將漕運商耗覈出二成，白糧覈出三成，由津局給價收買，隨正交運。 漕糧無故短少霉變，於備帶耗米內補足； 不敷，勒令買補。 如有斫桅松艙傷人等事則免之。 船戶腳價飯米折色並津貼等銀，先於受兌後發七成，餘三成交押運員弁，到壩後查無弊端，始行全發。 沙船餘米不下十萬石，初照南糧例，聽天津人照市價收買。 嗣以商人希圖賤價售買，改由官為收買，其價銀由江南委員轉發船戶，後仍令商船自行售賣。
In the sixth year's first month, grain transshipped by prefectures and counties reached Shanghai in turn for exchange and departed in batches. The sea route exceeded four thousand li; arrival came within ten-odd days. After grain reached Tongzhou, it went to capital granaries under inspection by civil and military officers of the Foot Soldiers command. Sand-boat wastage was drawn from the 180,000-odd shi issued to banner boatmen; the 60,000 shi saved was still dispatched with regular transport. For every shi of transported tribute, eight sheng of wastage was paid; for white grain, one dou—to supplement regular grain shortfalls. Two-tenths of merchant wastage on tribute grain and three-tenths on white grain were verified and purchased by the Tianjin bureau, then delivered with regular grain. If tribute grain was short or moldy without cause, it was made up from reserve wastage; if still insufficient, carriers were compelled to purchase and make it up. If masts were cut, cabins loosened, or people injured, they were exempted. Boat freight, rice allowance in silver, and Tianjin subsidies were paid seventy percent after exchange; the remaining thirty percent went to escort officers and was paid in full only after dam inspection found no abuse. Surplus sand-boat grain came to no less than one hundred thousand shi; at first Tianjin residents could buy at market price under the southern-grain precedent. Later, because merchants sought cheap purchase, the government bought instead; Jiangnan commissioners forwarded payment to boat households, and later merchant boats were again allowed to sell on their own.
60
每屆海運期，沿海水師提鎮，各按汛地，派撥哨船兵丁，巡防護送，並派武職大員二，隨船赴津。 上海交兌時，先期咨照浙江提鎮水師營出哨招寶、陳錢一帶地方，江南提鎮水師營出哨大小洋山，會於馬跡山，山東總鎮出哨成山、石島，會於鷹游門，以資彈壓。 山東洋面，責成游擊、守備，搜查島嶼，防護迎送。 後以邵燦言，停派護送武職大員，責成沿海水師逐程遞護。 嗣寧、滬商人各置火輪船一，遇新漕兌開行時，分別扼要巡防。
Each sea-transport season, coastal naval commanders assigned patrol boats and soldiers by station to escort grain, and two senior military officers went with the boats to Tianjin. At Shanghai exchange, Zhejiang's navy was notified to patrol Zhaobao and Chenqian, Jiangnan's to patrol Greater and Lesser Yangshan, meeting at Maji Shan; Shandong's regional commander patrolled Chengshan and Shidao, meeting at Yingyou Gate—to suppress disorder. On Shandong's coastal waters, patrol officers and garrison commanders searched islands and escorted grain. Later, at Shao Can's suggestion, senior military escorts were stopped; coastal naval forces escorted stage by stage. Later Ningbo and Shanghai merchants each kept one steamship to patrol key points when new tribute exchange opened.
61
剝船，直隸舊設二千五百艘，二百艘分撥故城等處，八百艘留楊村，餘千五百艘集天津備用。 後雇賝堪裝漕糧二百五十石民船五百艘，以備裝載。 商船首次抵津，先僅府縣倉腳廟宇撥卸三十萬石，餘令剝船徑運通倉。 隨將天津倉腳廟宇所儲漕米運通，無庸轉卸北倉，致多周折。 至商船二次抵津，如剝船不敷裝載，即將米先儲府縣倉腳廟宇； 不敷，再剝儲北倉。 隨令原剝將所儲米石侭數運通。 剝船足敷裝載，即按首次商船辦法，不必分儲北倉，以歸簡便。 剝船百六十隻為一起，由經紀自派人分起押運交倉，押運員役稟報倉場，復馳回續押後起米船。 經紀等止須帶領斛手到船起卸，如有藉端刁難需索，交地方官從嚴治罪。
Zhili originally maintained twenty-five hundred lighterage boats; two hundred went to Gucheng and elsewhere, eight hundred stayed at Yangcun, and fifteen hundred assembled at Tianjin. Later five hundred civilian boats capable of loading two hundred fifty shi each were hired as reserve. When merchant boats first reached Tianjin, only three hundred thousand shi were unloaded at prefectural, county, warehouse, and temple storage; the rest went directly by lighterage to Tongzhou. Grain stored at Tianjin warehouses and temples then went to Tongzhou without transshipment to the North Granary, avoiding extra steps. When merchant boats reached Tianjin a second time, if lighterage was insufficient, grain was first stored at prefectural, county, warehouse, and temple storage; if still insufficient, it was stored at the North Granary. Original lighterage crews were then ordered to transport all stored grain to Tongzhou. If lighterage sufficed, the first-arrival method was followed without separate North Granary storage, for simplicity. One hundred sixty lighterage boats formed one gang; brokers dispatched escorts by gang to deliver to granaries, reported to the granary office, and hurried back for the next gang. Brokers needed only to lead measuring hands to boats; if they created difficulties or made demands, local officials were to punish them severely.
62
各州縣經管剝船，每年例給修艌銀五兩，三年小修一次，給費二十兩，歲終漕竣，逐一挑驗，船身堅固者，酌量修艌，如損壞較甚，即核賞估價，所需經費，於道庫油艌銀項下動撥。 封河守凍期內，每船工食銀十五兩，運米百石，給腳價八兩四錢，食米一石一斗五升。 嗣每百石加腳費五兩。 李鴻章因官剝船戶貧困滋弊，例定工食銀十五兩，僅領一半，不敷贍家，請每船由蘇、浙漕項內酌貼五兩，部格不行。 鴻章上疏爭之，詔從其議。 商船領運漕糧，迅速無誤，萬石以下給匾額，五萬石獎職銜，每次奏保以百二三十人為限。
Prefectures and counties managing lighterage boats paid five liang repair silver annually; every three years minor repair cost twenty liang; after transport, boats were inspected—sound hulls were repaired as needed, badly damaged ones assessed and compensated from the circuit treasury's boat-oil repair account. During river freeze, each boat received fifteen liang for workers' food; per hundred shi, eight liang four qian porterage and one shi one dou five sheng food grain were paid. Later five liang porterage was added per hundred shi. Li Hongzhang, with official lighterage households growing poor and abuses multiplying, reported that regulated food silver of fifteen liang yielded only half, insufficient for families, and requested five liang per boat from Jiangsu and Zhejiang canal funds; the Board rejected it. Hongzhang protested in a further memorial; an edict approved his plan. Merchant boats transporting tribute swiftly and without error received inscribed plaques below ten thousand shi and official rank above fifty thousand shi; each promotion memorial was limited to 120 or 130 persons.
63
七年，蔣攸銛請新漕仍行海運。 上以近年河湖漸臻順軌，軍船可以暢行，不許。 其後各省歲運額漕，逐漸短少，太倉積粟，動放無存。 二十六年，詔復行海運。 二十七年，議准蘇、松、太二府一州漕白糧米，自明歲始，改由海運。 三十年，復令蘇、松、太二府一州白糧正耗米，援照成案，由海運津。 咸豐元年，戶部尚書孫瑞珍請河海並運。 御史張祥晉請將江蘇新漕，援案推廣常、鎮各屬及浙江，一體海運。 下江督陸建瀛、蘇撫楊文定、浙撫常大淳妥議。 覆稱明年蘇、松、常、鎮、太四府一州漕白糧米，請一律改由海運。 浙漕礙難海運，請仍循舊章，從之。 二年，建瀛上籌辦海運十事，下部議行。 是年以浙江漕船開兌過遲，回空不能依期歸次，詔來歲新漕改為海運，從巡撫黃宗漢請也。 五年，河決銅瓦廂，由張秋入大清河，挾汶東趨，運道益梗。 六年，截留江蘇應運漕糧二十萬石供支兵餉，實運漕白正耗及支賸給丁餘耗米七十五萬五千餘石，其歉緩南漕，令各州縣依限催徵運通。
In the seventh year, Jiang Youqian requested that new tribute still go by sea. The emperor, finding rivers and lakes increasingly navigable and military boats passing freely, did not permit it. Thereafter each province's annual quota gradually fell short, and Taicang's stored grain was quickly exhausted once drawn upon. In the twenty-sixth year, an edict restored sea transport. In the twenty-seventh year, white-grain tribute from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang was approved for sea transport from the following year. In the thirtieth year, regular and wastage white grain from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang was again ordered to Tianjin by sea under established precedent. In Xianfeng 1, Board of Revenue Minister Sun Ruizhen requested combined canal and sea transport. Censor Zhang Xiangjin requested extending Jiangsu's new-tribute precedent to Chang, Zhen, all jurisdictions, and Zhejiang—all by sea. Governor-General Lu Jianying, Governor Yang Wending, and Zhejiang Governor Chang Dachun were ordered to plan carefully. They replied that next year's white-grain tribute from Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Taicang should uniformly shift to sea transport. Zhejiang tribute could not easily go by sea; they requested old regulations. The edict approved. In the second year, Jianying memorialized ten items for organizing sea transport; the Board approved and implemented them. That year Zhejiang boats opened exchange too late and empty return missed schedule; an edict ordered next year's new tribute changed to sea transport at Governor Huang Zonghan's request. In the fifth year, the river breached at Tongwaxiang, entered the Daqing River at Zhangqiu, rushed east with the Wen, and the transport route grew more obstructed. In the sixth year, two hundred thousand shi of Jiangsu tribute due for transport were diverted for military rations; actual transport of white regular and wastage grain plus surplus for boatmen came to more than 755,000 shi; deferred southern tribute was ordered collected and sent to Tongzhou by prefectures and counties on deadline.
64
同治七年，議試用夾板船裝運採買米石，水腳銀數悉仍沙船例，給銀五錢五分，挽至天津紫竹林，由商董就近寄棧，聽驗米大臣會同通商大臣驗收過剝，所需小船剝價、棧租、挑力，每石給銀七分，由商董承領經理。 又每石給保險銀三分，設有遭風拋失，責令貼補。 至每米千石，隨耗八十石，備帶餘米二十石，剝船食耗米十一石五斗。 又每百石給津、通剝價銀八兩一錢四釐，通倉個兒錢折銀二兩，均照海運正漕採買各案辦理。 是年以津沽河面狹隘，常有沈船失米之虞，於大沽增設海運外局。
In the seventh year of Tongzhi, clipper boats were tried for purchased grain at sand-boat freight rates—five qian five fen per shi to Zizhulin in Tianjin, where merchant directors stored it for joint inspection and transshipment by the grain-inspection and treaty-port ministers; lighterage, warehouse rent, and porterage at seven fen per shi were managed by the merchant directors. Three fen of insurance silver per shi was also paid; storm losses had to be made up by the carriers. For every thousand shi, eighty shi of wastage, twenty shi of reserve surplus, and eleven shi five dou of lighterage food and wastage were provided. Per hundred shi, eight liang one qian four li of Tianjin-Tongzhou lighterage silver and two liang of Tongzhou handling silver were paid under the sea-transport regular-tribute and purchase cases. That year an outer sea-transport bureau was added at Dagu because the Tianjin river was narrow and boats often sank with their grain.
65
九年，浙江巡撫楊昌濬奏：「浙省來歲新漕，酌擬海運章程十四條：一，委員分辦，以專責成； 一，新漕仍由上海受兌放洋，白糧仍循案裝盛麻袋，首先運滬； 一，寬備海運商船，並由蘇省多撥沙船，移浙濟用； 一，經耗等米，仍照數支給，商耗飭帶本色並餘耗申糙等米搭交倉； 一，增給天津剝船耗米，以彌虧欠； 一，津、通經費，照案備帶，羨等款，仍按數抵解； 一，商船准帶砲械，並由商捐輪船護送，仍責成沿海水師實力巡防； 一，天津交米後，循舊責成經紀，續到之船，仍由天津道驗收； 一，循案加增海運經費； 一，米船到津，應多添排數，寬備剝船； 一，商船水腳等項，照案核給，並二成免稅，酌定賞罰； 一，商船二成免私之貨，仍以米石計斤，所帶竹木，照案免稅； 一，商船回空載貨，照向章免稅； 一，米船抵津交卸，嚴禁經紀斗斛剝船需索浮費。 」下部議行。 十年，鴻章言：「剝船守候苦累，每載米百石，請加給腳價銀五兩，並另籌運白糧民船守候口糧銀萬二千兩，由蘇、浙糧道庫漕項內撥解； 不敷，則由司庫通融借撥。 」
In the ninth year, Zhejiang governor Yang Changjun proposed fourteen articles for next year's sea transport: first, assign commissioners with fixed responsibility; second, new tribute grain will still be exchanged at Shanghai and sent to sea, with white grain in hemp sacks sent to Shanghai first as before; third, prepare merchant vessels broadly and transfer additional Jiangsu sand boats to assist Zhejiang; fourth, regulated wastage will still be issued in full; merchant wastage in kind, plus surplus wastage and declared coarse grain, will be delivered to the granary; fifth, increase Tianjin lighterage wastage grain to cover deficits; sixth, Tianjin and Tongzhou expenses will be carried as before, with surplus funds still delivered in full; seventh, merchant boats may carry arms and be escorted by merchant steamships, while coastal naval forces remain responsible for effective patrol; eighth, after delivery at Tianjin, brokers remain responsible as before and later boats will still be received by the Tianjin circuit intendant; ninth, increase sea-transport funds according to prior cases; tenth, when grain boats reach Tianjin, add berths and prepare lighterage boats broadly; eleventh, merchant freight and related items will be paid as before, with twenty-percent tax exemption and fixed rewards and penalties; twelfth, the twenty-percent tax-free private cargo will still be calculated by grain weight; bamboo and timber will be tax-free as before; thirteenth, return cargo on empty merchant boats will be tax-free as in former regulations; fourteenth, when grain boats reach Tianjin, brokers, measuring scoops, and lighterage boats are strictly forbidden to demand extra fees. The Board of Revenue approved and implemented the plan. In the tenth year, Hongzhang reported that lighterage crews suffered while waiting; he requested five liang more porterage silver per hundred shi, plus twelve thousand liang for civilian boats waiting on white grain, from Jiangsu and Zhejiang grain-route treasuries; if insufficient, the provincial treasury might lend flexibly. (Close of memorial.)
66
十一年，昌濬請以輪船運漕，從之。 輪船招商，由商人借領二十萬串為設局資本，盈虧悉由商任之。 購堅捷輪船三艘，每年撥海運漕米二十萬石，由招商輪船運津，其水腳耗米等項，仍照向章辦理。 輪船到津，命直督籌備剝船轉運，並會同倉場侍郎臨棧查驗，仍仿照白糧例，由江、浙撫道運通交納，以杜折耗偷漏。 輪船協運江、浙漕糧，簽明某省漕白糧米字樣於米袋之上。 糧米上棧時，由滬局派員監兌； 兌竣，即由輪船商局給收米迴文，以後裝船起運，俱由商局覈辦，滬局不再與聞。 其棧費夫力，亦由商局任之。 凡漕糧派裝輪船，輪船商局酌委執事，會同滬局詳驗，米色乾潔，方行收兌，交輪局押赴浦江東棧斛收。 抵津，飭津局各員董提前驗收，以免壅滯。 輪船每艘載米三千石，填發連單，由津局稽核，一切領銀領米等結悉罷之。 輪船運米，由上海道填給免稅執照，並援例得酌帶二成貨物。 其洋藥及二成之外另帶貨物，仍須納稅。
In the eleventh year, Changjun requested steamship transport. The request was approved. Merchants investing in steamships borrowed two hundred thousand strings of cash as bureau capital; profit and loss were entirely theirs. Three sturdy steamships were purchased; each year two hundred thousand shi of tribute grain went by merchant steamship to Tianjin, with freight and wastage still under former regulations. When steamships reached Tianjin, the Zhili governor-general prepared lighterage boats and, with the granary superintendent, inspected warehouses on site; delivery at Tongzhou still followed the white-grain precedent through Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors and intendants to prevent loss and theft. Merchant steamships assisting Jiangsu and Zhejiang tribute grain marked each bag with the province and white-grain designation. When grain went into warehouse, Shanghai bureau commissioners supervised exchange. After exchange, the steamship merchant bureau issued receipts; thereafter loading and dispatch were handled entirely by the merchant bureau, without the Shanghai bureau. Warehouse fees and labor were also borne by the merchant bureau. Whenever tribute grain was assigned to steamships, merchant-bureau clerks inspected jointly with Shanghai officers; only dry, clean grain was accepted and escorted to the Pudong warehouse east of the river for measuring and receipt. At Tianjin, bureau directors were ordered to inspect and receive in advance to avoid congestion. Each steamship carried three thousand shi; joint receipts were issued and audited by the Tianjin bureau, abolishing all former procedures for receiving silver and grain. The Shanghai circuit intendant issued tax-exemption licenses for steamship grain and, by precedent, allowed up to twenty percent of cargo in goods. Opium and any goods beyond twenty percent still had to pay tax.
67
喬松年奏山東境內黃水日益汎濫，運河淤塞，擬因勢利導，俾黃水先驅張秋。 其張秋南北，普行挑濬，修建徬壩以利漕。 丁寶楨、文彬奏請挽復淮、徐故道。 事下廷臣會議。 復稱銅瓦廂決後，舊河身淤墊過高，勢不能挽復淮、徐故道。 至借黃濟運，築堤束水，與導衛濟運之法同一難行。 鴻章奏請仍由海道轉運，令各省酌提本色若干運滬，由海船解津，餘照章折解，以節運費。 並隨時指撥漕折銀兩採買接濟，並請停止河運採買糧石，推廣海運。 仍下部議。 先是江北漕糧，由河運通，至是亦試辦海運。 十三年，奏准江西在滬採買漕糧八萬石，交招商局由海運津，每石腳價銀二兩七錢。 光緒元年，湖南漕糧採辦正耗米二萬三百四十五石，湖北採辦三萬石，均交招商局由海運津。 江西、湖南尋停。
Qiao Songnian reported that within Shandong the Yellow River was flooding more widely and the Grand Canal silting up; he proposed guiding the current to drive the river first toward Zhangqiu. North and south of Zhangqiu, broad dredging and embankment dams would benefit grain transport. Ding Baozhen and Wen Bin memorialized to restore the old Huai and Xu route. The matter was referred to court ministers for joint deliberation. They replied that after the Tongwaxiang breach the old riverbed had silted too high to restore the Huai-Xu route. Borrowing Yellow River water for transport and building dikes to confine it was as impracticable as guiding the Wei for transport. Hongzhang asked that transfer continue by sea, with each province sending set amounts of grain in kind to Shanghai for delivery to Tianjin, and the remainder commuted in silver to save costs. He also asked that commuted tribute silver be allocated to purchase grain as needed, that canal purchase stop, and sea transport expand. The matter was again referred to the Board of Revenue. Previously northern tribute grain had gone by canal to Tongzhou; now sea transport was tried as well. In the thirteenth year, Jiangxi was approved to purchase eighty thousand shi at Shanghai for delivery to Tianjin by China Merchants steamships at two liang seven qian per shi. In the first year of Guangxu, Hunan purchased 20,345 shi of regular and wastage grain and Hubei thirty thousand shi; both went to Tianjin by China Merchants steamships. Jiangxi and Hunan soon stopped.
68
寶楨奏運河廢壞，莫非黃水之害，治運必先治黃。 應先將微山湖之湖口雙閘及各減閘，迅速修砌，及時收蓄，以保湖瀦； 運河正身亦須量為疏濬。 嗣桂清、畢道遠、廣壽、賀壽慈等亦以籌款修復運河為請。 黃元善復稱：「自黃河北徙，運河阻滯，改由海運，原屬權宜之計。 當時奏定江蘇漕額，以河運經費作為海運支銷，每石不得過七錢。 嗣以經費不敷，迭次請增。 江蘇所加，距一兩不遠，浙江已加至一兩，較道光二十八年、咸豐二年海運經費尚有節省歸公者，大相逕庭。 且海運歷涉重洋，風波靡定，萬有不測，所關匪細。 河運雖迂滯，而沿途安定，經費維均。 自各省以達京倉，民之食其力者，不可數計。 裕國利民，計無善於此者。 現停運未久，及時修復，尚屬未晚。 再遲數年，河道日淤，需費更鉅。 臣以為河運迂而安，海運便而險，計出萬全，非復河運不可。 」上命河督、漕督及沿河各督撫籌畫具奏。 沈葆楨疏駁桂清、畢道遠等請將有漕省分酌提漕項及將海運糧石分出十數萬石改辦河運之議，並力言「河運決不能復。 運河旋濬旋淤，運方定章，河忽改道，河流不時遷徙，漕路亦隨為轉移。 而借黃濟運，為害尤烈。 前淤未盡，下屆之運已連檣接尾而至，高下懸殊，勢難飛渡。 於是百計逆水之性，強令就我範圍，致前修之款皆空，本屆之淤復積。 設令因濟運而奪溜，北趨則畿輔受其害，南趨則淮、徐受其害，億萬生靈，將有其魚之嘆，又不僅徒糜巨帑無裨漕運已也」。 七年，令直督飭招商局有協運漕糧時，酌分道員駐津驗兌，並責成糧道嚴督治漕事人員，兌米時加意查察。 因招商局協運江、浙漕糧，有攙雜破碎諸弊故也。
Baozhen reported that the Grand Canal's ruin was entirely the Yellow River's fault and that transport could be repaired only by repairing the river first. The lake-mouth double sluice at Weishan Lake and the various reduction sluices should quickly be rebuilt to store water and preserve the lake. The Grand Canal's main channel must also be dredged as needed. Later Gui Qing, Bi Daoyuan, Guang Shou, He Shouci, and others also requested funds to restore the canal. Huang Yuanshan again reported that since the Yellow River shifted north the canal had blocked and transport shifted to sea carriage as a temporary expedient. At that time Jiangsu tribute quotas were to use canal expenses for sea transport, not exceeding seven qian per shi. Later, because funds were insufficient, increases were requested again and again. Jiangsu's additions neared one liang per shi; Zhejiang had already reached one liang—far from the savings returned under Daoguang 28 and Xianfeng 2 sea-transport budgets. Moreover, sea transport crosses open water where winds and waves are uncertain—a serious risk. Canal transport, though slow, is stable along the route with evenly distributed costs. From every province to the capital granaries, countless people live by this labor. To enrich the state and benefit the people, no plan is better. Transport has been suspended only briefly; timely restoration is not yet too late. Wait a few years more and the channel will silt while costs grow ever greater. Canal transport is slow but safe, sea transport convenient but dangerous; for a fully secure plan, he argued, canal transport must be restored. The emperor ordered the river governor, grain-transport governor, and governors along the route to plan and report. Shen Baozhen opposed Gui Qing and Bi Daoyuan's proposals to draw tribute funds from grain provinces and divert sea-transport grain back to the canal, arguing strongly that canal transport could not be restored. The canal is dredged and silts again; transport rules are fixed, yet the river suddenly changes course and the grain route shifts with it. Borrowing Yellow River water for transport is especially harmful. Before one year's silt is cleared, the next fleet is already arriving stern to stern; with such a height difference, swift passage is impossible. Then every device forces the river against its nature into human design, wasting earlier repair funds while fresh silt accumulates. If diverting the current for transport steals the flow, a northward rush would harm the capital region and a southward rush Huai and Xu; countless lives would face ruin for vast sums wasted without helping transport. In the seventh year, whenever China Merchants assisted tribute transport, the Zhili governor-general was to station circuit officials at Tianjin to inspect exchange, and grain-route officials were to supervise handlers strictly. This followed adulteration, broken grain, and similar abuses in China Merchants' joint transport of Jiangsu and Zhejiang tribute.
69
十年，法人構釁，海運梗阻。 太常卿徐樹銘言：「漕糧宜全歸河運，請於運道經行處疏濬河流，修治閘壩，並選雇民船以濟運。 」明年，曾國荃言：「來年河運酌添江蘇漕糧五萬石，並將邳、宿河道淤淺處，酌估挑濬。 」從之。 盧士傑言：「鄭州黃河漫口奪溜，山東運河十里堡門外積淤日寬，回空漕船，不能挽抵口門。 現寧、蘇新漕待船裝載，邳、宿挑淤築壩，必待空船過竣，方可興工。 」上命迅飭疏濬積淤，俾漕船早日南下。 十五年，從山東巡撫張曜請，改撥海運漕米二十萬石仍歸河運。 曾國荃、黃彭年奏：「江、安河運米石，業經截留充賑。 蘇屬河運漕米十萬，前已改歸海運，各州縣起運，均已抵滬，驟改河運，窒礙難行。 且雇船將近千艘，亦非旦夕可致。 請俟本年冬漕，再行遵旨提前河運，以期規復舊章。 」制可。
In the tenth year, the French provoked hostilities and sea transport was obstructed. Grand Master of Ceremonies Xu Shuming reported that tribute grain should all return to canal transport, with rivers dredged, sluices repaired, and civilian boats hired along the route. The next year, Zeng Guoquan reported that next year's canal transport should add fifty thousand shi of Jiangsu tribute and that silted sections of the Pi-Su route should be dredged. The proposal was approved. Lu Shijie reported that at the Zhengzhou breach the current was diverted; outside Shimenbao on the Shandong canal silt widened daily and empty tribute boats could not reach the sluice mouth. Ningbo and Suzhou new tribute awaited boats for loading, while Pi-Su dredging and dam-building had to wait until empty boats passed. The emperor ordered swift dredging so tribute boats could return south early. In the fifteenth year, at Zhang Yao's request, two hundred thousand shi reassigned from sea to canal transport were returned to the canal. Zeng Guoquan and Huang Pengnian reported that Jiangsu and Anhui canal grain had already been diverted for famine relief. One hundred thousand shi of Jiangsu canal tribute, already reassigned to sea transport and dispatched to Shanghai, could not suddenly return to the canal. Nearly a thousand hired boats could not be assembled overnight. They asked to follow the edict for this winter's transport and shift to early canal transport next year to restore the old regulations. The edict approved.
70
十九年，北運河上游潮、白等河狂漲，水勢高於堤顛數尺，原築上堰，俱沒水中，運河水旱大小決口七十餘處，由津運京米麥雜糧千數百艘，在楊村阻淺，命鴻章將各口門堵合，並疏濬河身，停蓄水勢，以利舟行。 二十二年，王文韶奏：「南漕改行海運，惟江北漕糧仍由河運，復於蘇、松項下提撥米十萬石併入河運。 船多道遠，自黃入運，自運入衛，節節阻滯，船戶窮無復之，竊米攙水，諸弊叢生。 本年漕船到津，較昔已遲二三月，誠恐有誤回空。 已飭並程催趲，剋日兌收。 但此次截留江北漕米五萬石，米色尚佳。 江蘇五萬石，米色參差，甚或蒸變，剔除晾曬，幾費周章，蓋運受黃病，已非人力所能挽救。 擬請自本年始，改撥蘇漕之十萬石統歸海運。 其江蘇冬漕仍辦河運，以保運道。 」下部議行。 御史秦夔揚以江北河運勞費太甚，疏請停辦，改折解部。 部議漕糧關係京倉儲積，未便遽更舊制。
In the nineteenth year, the Chao, Bai, and other upstream rivers on the North Canal rose violently, standing several chi above the dikes; more than seventy breaches opened; thousands of boats from Tianjin to the capital were stranded at Yangcun. Hongzhang was ordered to block the breaches, dredge the channel, and hold water for navigation. In the twenty-second year, Wang Wenshao reported that southern tribute had shifted to sea transport while northern tribute still went by canal, with another hundred thousand shi from Suzhou and Songjiang added to canal transport. Boats were many and the route long; from the Yellow River into the canal and from the canal into the Wei, every stage brought obstruction; desperate boat households stole grain and adulterated with water, and abuses multiplied. This year's boats reached Tianjin two or three months late; missing the empty return was a real fear. Orders were already issued to press forward and receive exchange on schedule. But the fifty thousand shi of northern tribute held back this time were still of good color. The fifty thousand shi from Jiangsu varied in color; some had steamed and spoiled and required sorting and drying at great trouble—the harm of Yellow River water was beyond human remedy. He proposed that from that year the hundred thousand shi of Suzhou tribute be reassigned entirely to sea transport. Jiangsu winter tribute would still go by canal to preserve the route. The Board of Revenue approved and implemented the plan. Censor Qin Kuiyang, finding northern canal transport too costly, memorialized to stop it and commute delivery to the Board of Revenue in silver. The Board replied that tribute grain concerned capital reserves and the old system should not be changed hastily.
71
二十六年，以戰端既開，從陳璧請，於清江浦設漕運總局。 車駕西幸，轉運局移漢口，清江改設分局。 是年南漕改用火車由津運京。 二十七年，以財用匱乏，諭：「自本年始，直省河運海運，一律改徵折色，責成各省大吏清釐整頓，節省局費運費，並查明各州縣徵收浮費，勒令繳出歸公，以期匯成巨款。 」奕劻請於應辦白糧外，每年採辦漕糧百萬石，純用粳米，並不得率請截留，從之。 二十八年，部議本年江、浙漕糧，純歸招商局輪船承運，費應力從減省。 盛宣懷奏：「近年滬局輪船，因事起運太遲，棧耗既鉅，及運至塘沽，又值聯軍未退，費用倍於常時。 二十六、二十七兩年，招商局所領水腳，實不敷所出。 本年太古洋行原減價攬載，英、日議定商約，均欲漕運列入約章，臣等力拒之。 蓋招商局為中國公司，前李鴻章奏准漕米、軍米悉歸招商局承運，實寓有深意也。 此次詳察中外情形，擬請自二十八年冬漕始，於向章每石輪船水腳保險等項漕米銀三錢八分八釐一毫內減去五分，永為定制。 」從之。
In the twenty-sixth year, because war had begun, a grain-transport general bureau was established at Qingjiangpu at Chen Bi's request. When the court moved west, the transfer bureau moved to Hankou and a branch bureau was set up at Qingjiang. That year southern tribute grain was carried by rail from Tianjin to the capital. In the twenty-seventh year, with finances exhausted, an edict declared that from that year onward canal and sea transport in every province would be converted to silver commutation. Governors were charged with clearing accounts, cutting bureau and transport costs, and forcing prefectures and counties to surrender excessive levies to the treasury. Yikuang asked that, besides white grain still required, one million shi of tribute grain be purchased annually in polished rice alone, with no casual diversions. The request was approved. In the twenty-eighth year, the Board of Revenue decided that Jiangsu and Zhejiang tribute grain for that year would be carried entirely by China Merchants steamships, with costs cut as far as possible. Sheng Xuanhuai memorialized that in recent years Shanghai steamships had sailed too late, causing heavy warehouse loss, and that at Tanggu the allied armies had not yet withdrawn, doubling normal costs. In the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh years, freight paid to China Merchants fell short of actual costs. That year Butterfield & Swire underbid for the cargo; Britain and Japan both sought to include grain transport in commercial treaties, but the court firmly resisted. China Merchants is a Chinese company; when Li Hongzhang had earlier secured tribute and military grain for it, he had done so with deliberate purpose. After reviewing conditions at home and abroad, he proposed that from the twenty-eighth year's winter transport, five fen be permanently cut from the established per-shi steamship freight, insurance, and related tribute-grain charge of three qian eight fen eight li one hao. The proposal was approved.
72
江、浙漕糧由海運津，向用剝船運至通倉，每石支耗米一升一合五勺，名曰「津剝食耗」。 自南漕改用火車運京，此項耗米，改令隨正交倉。 嗣因運米事竣，每有虧耗，許仍舊支給，以抵車運虧耗云。
Jiangsu and Zhejiang tribute grain sent by sea to Tianjin had been carried onward to Tongzhou by lighterage boats, with one sheng one he five shao of wastage grain per shi, called "Tianjin lighterage food wastage." Once southern tribute grain went by rail to the capital, this wastage allowance was ordered delivered with the regular grain. Later, because transport often ended with shortfalls, the old allowance was again permitted to offset losses on rail transport.
